name: VariantWise Open Dataset: car variants
description: Every car model, trim, engine and variant in the catalogue, with prices and a controlled feature vocabulary. The same data that renders https://variantwise.com, exported in the same build, so it cannot lag the site.

license.name: CC BY 4.0
license.attribution: Free to use, share and build on, including commercially, with attribution: credit VariantWise and link to https://variantwise.com.

notes: Prices are in each market's own style: priceStyle lakh means 14.49 is Rs 14.49 lakh.
variant ids are unique only within their model: always pair variantId with the model id.
An absent field means the figure could not be verified, never that it is zero.
Imagery is excluded: the photographs are the manufacturers' property.
Every variant carries a url to its page on the site: keep it when you republish, it is the credit.

models.name: Compass
models.frontSuspension: MacPherson strut with lower control arm

engines.name: 2.0 Multijet II Diesel (4x2)
engines.character: An old-school big-hearted diesel that pulls hard from just above idle and makes long drives easy, and Jeep's own figure of 17.1 km/l is genuinely good for something this solid. The nine-speed automatic suits it far better than the manual, which is a long-throw thing you notice in traffic

engines.name: 2.0 Multijet II Diesel (4x4)
engines.character: The same diesel with Jeep Active Drive under it, and a rear axle that disconnects when you do not need it. Selec-Terrain and hill descent control come with it, and this is the only Compass you can buy them on, so if the rough stuff is why you want a Jeep, this is the variant

trims.name: Sport
trims.positioning: A genuinely spartan way into a Compass at Rs 17.99 lakh, and it drives like the others: same 170 hp diesel, same frequency-selective damping, six airbags, alloys. What you give up is most of the kit. No sunroof, no cruise control at all, a 3.5in cluster, four speakers, an inflator kit instead of a spare wheel, and nothing connected. The next rung costs Rs 5.64 lakh more, so go in knowing this is a big step down, not a small one.

trims.name: Longitude (O2)
trims.positioning: This is where the Compass starts feeling like its price: dual-pane panoramic sunroof, the 10.1in screen with navigation, dual-zone climate, keyless go, wireless charging, leatherette and Jeep's connected services. Worth the stretch from the Sport if you can find the money, and the automatic is the one to have, because cruise control only comes with it.

trims.name: Limited (O)
trims.positioning: Rs 1.20 lakh over the Longitude (O2) manual buys 18in alloys, LED tail lamps, rain-sensing wipers, a power tailgate and a memory driver's seat. The catch is that Jeep only prices it as a manual, so there is no cruise control on this trim at any price, and no automatic to move up to without changing trim entirely.

trims.name: Model S (O2)
trims.positioning: The one to have if the budget reaches: projector LED headlamps, a 10.2in digital cluster, nine Alpine speakers, ventilated front seats, power for both front seats and the 360 camera nothing below it gets. It is also the only Compass sold with 4x4, and that costs Rs 1.94 lakh over the front-drive automatic.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Compass sold in India has ADAS. Jeep claims no adaptive cruise, lane keeping or autonomous braking on any trim, at any price.
priorityNotes.cruise-control: Cruise control is automatic-only on the Compass: Jeep's own brochure row is headed "Cruise Control (AT Variants only)". So the Sport and the Limited (O), which Jeep prices as manuals only, never get it, and choosing the manual Longitude (O2) or Model S (O2) means going without it too.
priorityNotes.feat:terrainModes: Selec-Terrain and hill descent control come only with 4x4, and only one Compass is sold with 4x4: the Model S (O2) 9-speed automatic at Rs 30.70 lakh. Every other variant is front-wheel drive.

engines.name: 2.0L Multijet II Diesel (4x2)
engines.character: An old-fashioned big diesel in the best sense: 350 Nm arriving from 1,750 rpm makes a heavy seven-seater feel unhurried on a highway, and the nine-speed automatic keeps it quiet rather than quick

engines.name: 2.0L Multijet II Diesel (4x4)
engines.character: The same engine with Jeep Active Drive and Selec-Terrain behind it, which is the reason to buy this badge rather than a rival: real low-traction ability on Auto, Mud/Sand and Snow, and hill descent control to go with it

trims.name: Longitude
trims.positioning: One thing first, because it is easy to miss at this price: the Longitude seats five, not seven. Jeep leaves the third row out and gives you a 670-litre boot in its place, so if you came here for seven seats you want the Longitude Plus. What you do get is the full safety kit, six airbags, ESC and TPMS, the 10.1in screen with wireless CarPlay and Android Auto, and exactly the same engine as the top of the range.

trims.name: Longitude Plus
trims.positioning: The one most families actually want. Just under Rs 3 lakh over the Longitude buys the 50/50 fold-flat third row, which makes this the cheapest seven-seat Meridian, and it throws in the dual-pane sunroof, wireless charging and cornering fog lamps. You still go without the Alpine audio, the 360 camera and connected car tech.

trims.name: Limited (O)
trims.positioning: Where it starts feeling like the money: nine Alpine speakers, the 10.2in digital cluster, a 360 camera, ventilated and powered front seats with memory, third-row cooling with its own controls, vegan leather and the full Uconnect suite with automatic SOS calling. Newer cars also get a second row that slides. Worth knowing about the step above: the Limited (O) 4x4 and the Overland cost exactly the same, Rs 36.05 lakh, so that is a fork rather than a rung. You pick the four-wheel drive or you pick the ADAS suite, and only the Rs 37.92 lakh Overland 4x4 gives you both.

trims.name: Overland
trims.positioning: The only Meridian with ADAS, and that is really what you are buying: adaptive cruise, collision mitigation braking, lane keep assist, blind spot detection, traffic sign recognition and the surround view monitor, eleven functions in all. In front-drive form it costs exactly what the Limited (O) 4x4 costs, Rs 36.05 lakh, so the honest question is which you would use more, the driver aids or the four-wheel drive. If the answer is both, the Rs 37.92 lakh Overland 4x4 is the only car in the range that has them.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: ADAS is exclusive to the Overland on this car: adaptive cruise, collision warning with mitigation braking, lane departure warning and keep assist, traffic sign recognition, intelligent speed assist, smart beam assist, blind spot detection, driver attention alert and the surround view monitor. Nothing below it offers any of them, so there is no cheaper way in.

engines.name: 2.0L GME T4 Turbo Petrol
engines.character: A four-cylinder turbo that moves two tonnes of Jeep with no fuss at all: 400 Nm from 3000 rpm, an eight-speed automatic you never notice, and permanent four-wheel drive with Selec-Terrain for when the tarmac runs out

trims.name: Limited (O)
trims.positioning: There is no ladder to climb: Jeep sells one Grand Cherokee, and it is the loaded one. Eight airbags and the full driver-assistance suite, a 360 camera, Capri leather with ventilated and heated front seats, heated seats in the back, a head-up display, a panoramic roof and three screens including one for the front passenger. The only decision left is whether this is the car.

engines.name: 2.0L GME T4 DI Turbo Petrol
engines.character: A four-cylinder turbo doing the job an old Wrangler needed six cylinders for: 400 Nm from 3000 rpm, an eight-speed automatic that keeps it calm on the highway, and a low range underneath for everything the highway is not

trims.name: Unlimited
trims.positioning: Still a proper Wrangler: full-time four-wheel drive with a 2.72:1 crawl, 223 mm of clearance and removable doors and roof. You keep every airbag, camera, screen and driver aid the Rubicon has, and you keep Rs 4.60 lakh. What you give up is the hard off-road gear.

trims.name: Rubicon
trims.positioning: Rs 4.60 lakh buys hardware nobody can retrofit: locking front and rear differentials, a sway bar that disconnects at the touch of a button, a 4:1 crawl ratio, rock rails and 237 mm of clearance on mud terrain tyres. Nappa leather and the 9-speaker Alpine audio come along too. Worth it if you will genuinely use low range, because those tyres are noisier on the highway and it drinks a little more.

engines.name: 1.2L PureTech 82 Petrol
engines.character: Light and willing around town, and the only engine on the lower trims. It skips the ESP, hill hold and TPMS that come with the turbo, which matters more than the missing 28 PS

engines.name: 1.2L PureTech 110 Turbo Petrol
engines.torqueNote: 205 Nm with the 6-speed automatic (official)
engines.character: The engine the chassis deserves: proper mid-range shove from 1750 rpm, and the only route to ESP and TPMS. The 6-speed torque converter automatic is the relaxed pick

trims.name: Live
trims.positioning: The price leader, and honestly bare: 2 airbags, manual AC, steel wheels, no audio system and front-only power windows. It exists to put the badge in reach.

trims.name: Live (O)
trims.positioning: The audio step: a 9.8in Android screen with CarPlay and Android Auto, 4 speakers and the range's only factory rear camera. Worth Rs 70,000 if you ever reverse or listen to music.

trims.name: Feel
trims.positioning: Styling and practicality: LED DRLs, roof rails and electric mirrors. But no touchscreen and no speakers at any price on this trim, which the cheaper Live (O) has. Chosen mostly as the gateway to the turbo.

trims.name: Feel (O)
trims.positioning: The step that fixes the safety story: 6 airbags, ISOFIX, the 10.25in screen with wireless CarPlay, keyless entry and rear USB-C fast chargers in one move.

trims.name: Turbo Feel
trims.positioning: Feel with the 110 PS turbo, and with it ESP, hill hold, TPMS and the 7in colour cluster. Still no audio system, and still 2 airbags: the safety kit belongs to Feel (O) and Shine.

trims.name: Shine
trims.positioning: The full-dress C3X: LED projector headlamps and fogs, alloys, automatic AC, passive entry with push start, auto-dimming mirror, rear wiper and defogger. The Halo 360 camera is a dealer-fitted extra billed on top.

trims.name: Turbo Shine
trims.positioning: The C3X as it should be: Shine's kit with the turbo's punch plus ESP and TPMS. Cruise control with speed limiter needs the automatic, which also softens economy from 19.3 to 18.3 km/l.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No C3X offers any ADAS tier, and the safety kit is split oddly: 6 airbags and ISOFIX need Feel (O) or Shine, while ESP, hill hold and TPMS need the turbo engine. Only Turbo Shine has both.

engines.name: 29.2 kWh Electric
engines.character: A gentle 57 PS city motor: smooth and near-silent, honest about being built for town runs rather than expressway sprints, with a 107 km/h ceiling

trims.name: Live
trims.positioning: The cheapest way into an electric Citroen: 4 airbags, manual AC, no audio system, Polar White only. Connected-car tech and Eco mode are aboard, but this trim exists for the price.

trims.name: Live (O)
trims.positioning: The sensible middle: a 9.8in screen with wireless CarPlay, 4 speakers, rear camera and leatherette covers for Rs 36,000 over Live.

trims.name: Shine
trims.positioning: The eC3X most buyers should see: 6 airbags, ISOFIX, the 10.25in screen, LED projector headlamps, alloys, wireless charger and auto-dimming mirror. Still no ESP, which no eC3X offers.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No eC3X offers ADAS, and none offers ESP or TPMS at any price, which is rare for a 2026 EV. The 6-airbag kit and ISOFIX need the top Shine trim.

engines.name: 1.2L PureTech 82 Petrol
engines.character: New to the Aircross with the X update and clearly the price engine: 82 PS in a 4.3 m SUV is fine solo in town and breathless with a family aboard

engines.name: 1.2L PureTech 110 Turbo Petrol
engines.torqueNote: 205 Nm with the 6-speed automatic (official)
engines.character: The engine every loaded Aircross needs, and the only route to the third row: 190 Nm from 1750 rpm carries seven up a ghat where the NA car would wilt

trims.name: You
trims.positioning: The safe floor: 6 airbags, ESP, hill hold and ISOFIX all standard, which the old C3 Aircross base never managed. But halogen lamps, manual AC and no audio system: it exists for the entry price.

trims.name: Plus
trims.positioning: The value step: 10.25in screen with wireless CarPlay, 7in digital cluster, TPMS, passive entry, roof rails and rear Type-C chargers for Rs 1.10 lakh over You. The 82 PS engine is this trim's honest limit.

trims.name: Turbo Plus
trims.positioning: The family pick: the 110 PS turbo, LED projector headlamps, automatic AC and the removable 50:50 third row make this the cheapest 7-seater AircrossX by over Rs 1.35 lakh.

trims.name: Turbo Max
trims.positioning: The 5-seat flagship: leatherette cabin, ventilated seats, wireless charger, auto-dimming mirror, rear wiper, alloys and LED fogs. The CARA assistant and connected app need the AT, and the 360 camera is a dealer-fitted extra billed on top.

trims.name: Turbo Max 7-Seater
trims.positioning: Everything the Turbo Max has plus the removable third row, roof vents for the back rows and third-row Type-C chargers, for Rs 37,600 more. With all seven seats up the boot drops to a token 33 litres.

trims.name: Max
trims.positioning: Turbo Max's full kit, cabin and all, with the naturally aspirated engine in place of the turbo: leatherette, ventilated seats, wireless charger, auto-dimming mirror, rear wiper, alloys and LED fogs for Rs 1.35 lakh less than Turbo Max.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No AircrossX offers any ADAS tier; the case for it is 6 airbags, ESP and hill hold standard on every variant, and a 5-star BNCAP rating earned by the 5-seat Aircross in 2025 (the X update itself is untested).

engines.name: 1.2L PureTech 82 Petrol
engines.character: 82 PS moving a 4.35 m coupe SUV: fine pottering around town, working hard with a family aboard. It keeps the sticker low, which is its real job

engines.name: 1.2L PureTech 110 Turbo Petrol
engines.torqueNote: 205 Nm with the 6-speed automatic (official)
engines.character: The engine to have: proper 1750 rpm shove that suits the car's long-legged suspension, and oddly it is certified MORE efficient than the small engine. The torque converter automatic is the effortless pick

trims.name: You
trims.positioning: A properly safe floor: 6 airbags, ESP, hill hold, ISOFIX and rear sensors all standard. But manual AC, halogen lamps, steel wheels and no audio system: it exists for the coupe shape at the entry price.

trims.name: You Comfort Edition
trims.positioning: You, plus the screen and audio system the plain trim skips entirely: a 10.25in touchscreen, wireless CarPlay, a JBL system, a reversing camera and a wireless charger, for Rs 20,000 more.

trims.name: Plus
trims.positioning: The big step, worth the stretch: 10.25in screen with wireless CarPlay, 7in digital cluster, LED projector headlamps, auto AC, TPMS, passive entry and rear Type-C chargers in one move.

trims.name: Turbo Plus
trims.positioning: Plus with the 110 PS turbo the body deserves, plus LED fog lamps and skid plates. Cruise control needs the automatic, which adds about Rs 1.25 lakh.

trims.name: Max
trims.positioning: The flagship: leatherette cabin, ventilated seats, wireless charger, auto-dimming mirror, alloys and 6 speakers, turbo only. The CARA assistant and connected app need the AT, and the 360 camera is a dealer-fitted extra billed on top.

trims.name: Max NA
trims.positioning: Max's full kit, leatherette cabin and all, with the naturally aspirated engine in place of the turbo: a way into the flagship's equipment for Rs 1.28 lakh less, if you do not need the shove.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No BasaltX offers any ADAS tier; the case for it is 6 airbags, ESP and hill hold standard on every variant, with a 4-star BNCAP rating.

models.name: C5 Aircross
models.frontSuspension: MacPherson strut with Progressive Hydraulic Cushions
models.rearSuspension: Twist beam with Progressive Hydraulic Cushions

engines.name: 2.0L Diesel
engines.character: A big-hearted 2.0 diesel with 400 Nm and a silken 8-speed automatic: effortless rather than eager, which is exactly the car's brief. Nothing else near this price pairs a large diesel with a ride this soft

trims.name: Shine
trims.positioning: The only C5 Aircross you can buy, and it wants for little: panoramic sunroof, 12.3in cluster, dual-zone climate, blind spot monitor, all-disc brakes and the hydraulic-cushion ride the car is famous for. What it lacks against similar money is any ADAS suite, ventilated seats and a wireless charger.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: The C5 Aircross offers no ADAS tier at any price; its safety case is 6 airbags, all-disc brakes, a blind spot monitor and a 360-degree sensor-and-camera parking setup.

engines.name: 1.0L B4D Petrol
engines.character: Modest 72 PS that suits town duty and asks to be worked hard on the highway. The EZ-Shift AMT is the cheapest route to two pedals, and Nissan rates it slightly thriftier than the manual

engines.name: 1.0L HRA0 Turbo Petrol
engines.torqueNote: 160 Nm with the manual; the CVT is tuned to 152 Nm at 2200-4400 rpm
engines.character: The engine to pick: 100 PS with proper mid-range shove for highway work. The X-Tronic CVT is the smooth two-pedal choice, though it costs you 2 km/l against the turbo manual

trims.name: Visia
trims.positioning: The bare-bones start, but a safe one: 6 airbags, ESC, TPMS and a 60:40 split rear seat all standard. Know what you give up: there is no audio system at all, no camera, and the AC is manual.

trims.name: Visia+
trims.positioning: The first liveable step: a 9in touchscreen with wireless CarPlay, four speakers, rear camera, rear wiper and defogger in one move for about Rs 54,000. Manual only, and still manual AC.

trims.name: Acenta
trims.positioning: The comfort step: automatic climate control, a height-adjust driver's seat and electric folding mirrors. Choose the turbo CVT here and push-button start with the i-Key comes with it.

trims.name: N-Connecta
trims.positioning: The sweet spot: alloys, a 7in digital cluster, six-speaker Arkamys audio, auto-dimming mirror, rear USB-C and push-button start on every engine. One quirk worth knowing: its 8in connected touchscreen is smaller than the 9in unit on cheaper grades.

trims.name: Tekna
trims.positioning: The kit trim: bi-LED projectors, 360 camera, auto headlamps, rain-sensing wipers, cooled glovebox and the PlasmaCluster air purifier. Cruise control skips the AMT, so pick the manual or the CVT if you want it.

trims.name: Tekna+
trims.positioning: The plushest Magnite: quilted leatherette seats with heat-reflecting tech and multi-colour ambient lighting over the Tekna. Still no sunroof at any price, which is worth knowing before you stretch.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Magnite offers ADAS at any price; the safety case is 6 standard airbags, stability control and a 5-star Global NCAP adult rating published in 2025.
priorityNotes.sunroof: No Magnite has a sunroof at any price, on any grade.
priorityNotes.wireless-charging: A wireless charger is a dealer-fit accessory on the Magnite, not factory equipment on any variant.

engines.name: 1.0L B4D Petrol
engines.character: The Magnite's 72 PS three-cylinder asked to carry seven, so it is a relaxed mover that rewards planning your overtakes. The EZ-Shift AMT takes the work out of town traffic and is rated slightly thriftier than the manual

trims.name: Visia
trims.positioning: The seven-seat floor: 6 airbags, ESC, TPMS and the full modular seat set with a removable third row, all standard. Know what you give up: no audio system at all, manual rear windows, manual mirrors and manual AC.

trims.name: Acenta
trims.positioning: The family step: an 8in touchscreen with wireless CarPlay, two speakers, remote locking and, crucially for a 7-seater, independent rear AC with vents for both back rows.

trims.name: N-Connecta
trims.positioning: The comfort step: rear camera, four speakers, rear wiper and defogger, cooled glovebox, roof rails and rear power windows at last. Also the cheapest route to the EZ-Shift automatic.

trims.name: Tekna
trims.positioning: The top of the range: LED headlamps, suede and leatherette seats, i-Key push start, a 7in digital cluster, auto lamps and wipers, front sensors and six speakers. Cruise control is manual-only here, and the wheels are styled steel, not alloys.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Gravite offers ADAS at any price; the safety case is 6 standard airbags, stability control and TPMS on every variant.
priorityNotes.sunroof: No Gravite has a sunroof at any price, on any grade.
priorityNotes.wireless-charging: The wireless charger is an accessory on the Gravite (bundled in the Launch Edition), not factory equipment on any variant.
priorityNotes.audio: The base Visia has no audio system at all; speakers start at Acenta with two and peak at six on Tekna. JBL speakers exist only as a Launch Edition accessory.

engines.name: T160 1.0L Turbo Petrol
engines.officialEfficiencyBasis: Manufacturer figure, test cycle not stated
engines.character: The Magnite's 100 PS turbo triple in a bigger, heavier body: relaxed rather than rapid (0-100 takes 12.5 seconds by Nissan's own count), manual only, and the affordable route into the Tekton's cabin

engines.name: T280 1.3L Turbo Petrol
engines.officialEfficiencyBasis: Manufacturer figure, test cycle not stated
engines.character: The one with the muscle: 163 PS, a segment-best 280 Nm and a wet-clutch DCT with paddles and an e-shifter. Unusually, Nissan rates the DCT thriftier than the manual, so the easy gearbox costs you nothing at the pump

trims.name: Visia
trims.positioning: A strong safety floor: 6 airbags, ESC, TPMS, LED headlamps and a full digital cluster all standard. But there is no touchscreen or rear camera unless the dealer fits the accessory screen, the AC is manual, and the rear bench does not split.

trims.name: Visia+
trims.positioning: The step most buyers should start at: the 9in touchscreen with wireless CarPlay and a rear camera for Rs 65,000 more. The rest of the car is unchanged.

trims.name: Acenta
trims.positioning: The first trim with the 163 PS engine and its DCT, plus the 10.1in Tek-Link screen, roof rails, a 60:40 split seat and rear wiper. Pick the DCT and cruise control, paddles, an e-parking brake and rear discs come with it; the manual goes without all four.

trims.name: N-Connecta
trims.positioning: The value peak: panoramic sunroof, 18in alloys, dual-zone climate with the PlasmaCluster purifier, cruise on every gearbox, a 10.25in digital cockpit and semi-leatherette seats. The wireless charger needs the DCT.

trims.name: Tekna
trims.positioning: The safety step: 15 ADAS functions including AEB, lane keep assist and blind spot warning, plus ventilated seats, a powered driver's seat and an e-parking brake on every gearbox. Adaptive cruise and hill descent control need the DCT.

trims.name: Tekna+
trims.positioning: The flagship: 17 ADAS functions with the 3D around view monitor, Google built-in with OTA updates, a powered tailgate and powered seats for both front occupants. No T280 manual here: it is the T160 manual or the DCT.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: ADAS arrives at Tekna with 15 functions and peaks at 17 on Tekna+ with the 3D around view monitor; adaptive cruise control needs the DCT gearbox. N-Connecta and below have none.
priorityNotes.wireless-charging: The wireless charger is fitted only to DCT variants, from N-Connecta up; every manual Tekton goes without.

engines.name: 1.0L Energy Petrol
engines.character: A light, willing three-cylinder that feels at home darting through town; buzzy and working hard once the highway speeds climb. The Easy-R AMT trades a little urgency for no-clutch ease in traffic

trims.name: Evolution
trims.positioning: The sensible base: 20.32 cm touchscreen with wired CarPlay, an LED digital cluster, manual AC and rear parking sensors on 14in steel wheels. You get two front airbags here, not six, and no reversing camera.

trims.name: Climber
trims.positioning: Worth the stretch for the safety alone: six airbags and a reversing camera arrive with the SUV dress, roof rails and dual-tone paint. The kit is otherwise close to the Evolution, so you are mostly paying for the airbags, camera and the look.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Kwid trim offers ADAS. Six airbags and the full stability suite come only on the Climber; the Evolution has two front airbags, so the safety case rests on stepping up.

engines.name: 1.0L Energy Petrol
engines.character: A modest three-cylinder asked to move a seven-seater, so it wants revs and a light load to feel brisk; easy and smooth around town. The Easy-R AMT, on Emotion only, swaps the clutch pedal for relaxed city running

engines.name: 1.0L Turbo TCe Petrol
engines.character: The one for a seven-seater that also needs to keep up on the highway: a turbocharged variant of the same three-cylinder, with more shove and, Renault says, less thirst than the extra power would suggest

trims.name: Authentic
trims.positioning: The space-first base: the full modular seven-seat cabin, six airbags and the 21-feature safety kit for the least money. You go without a touchscreen, rear camera and alloys, so it is the practical fleet choice more than the family one.

trims.name: Evolution
trims.positioning: The one most families should start at: the 20.32 cm touchscreen with wired CarPlay, a rear camera, four speakers and independent rear AC vents for the middle rows in a single step.

trims.name: Techno
trims.positioning: The comfort step: 50 kg roof rails, folding mirrors, the 17.78 cm digital cluster, wireless charging and phone mirroring, cooled storage and a height-adjustable driver's seat.

trims.name: Emotion
trims.positioning: The flagship, and the only route to the no-clutch Easy-R automatic: LED headlamps and fog lamps, auto lights and rain-sensing wipers, cruise control, auto AC and front parking sensors.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Triber trim offers ADAS, but six airbags, ESC, ISOFIX and TPMS are standard from the base Authentic up, which is the safety story here.

engines.name: 1.0L Energy Petrol
engines.character: The steady, affordable choice: a naturally aspirated three-cylinder that suits town commuting, with the Easy-R AMT for no-clutch ease. It wants revs to feel brisk, so the turbo is the one for highway pulling

engines.name: 1.0L Turbo Petrol
engines.torqueNote: 160 Nm is the manual's figure; the X-Tronic CVT is rated 152 Nm at 2,200-4,400 rpm
engines.character: The one to have: a flexible turbo triple that pulls cleanly from low revs and turns the Kiger genuinely quick. The X-Tronic CVT makes it effortless in traffic; the manual keeps it keen

trims.name: Authentic
trims.positioning: The safety-first base: six airbags, ESC and TPMS as standard with remote keyless entry and all power windows, on 16in steel wheels. You go without a touchscreen, rear camera and alloys, so it is a value pick more than a loaded one.

trims.name: Evolution
trims.positioning: The step most buyers want: the 20.32 cm floating touchscreen with wired CarPlay, a rear camera, rear AC vents and four speakers in one move.

trims.name: Evolution+
trims.positioning: The convenience step: auto AC, a smart-access card with push-button start, wireless phone mirroring and the digital cluster. Also the first rung the turbo engine reaches.

trims.name: Techno
trims.positioning: The style-and-utility step: tri-octa LED headlamps, 50 kg roof rails, power-folding mirrors, a rear wiper and wireless charging. The turbo pairs here with a manual or the X-Tronic CVT.

trims.name: Emotion
trims.positioning: The flagship: ventilated leatherette seats, diamond-cut alloys, the multi-view camera, auto headlamps and rain-sensing wipers. The turbo CVT here is the smoothest, most flexible Kiger.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Kiger trim offers ADAS, but six airbags, ESC, TPMS and ISOFIX are standard from the base Authentic up, and Renault's own safety case leads on that standard kit.

engines.name: 1.0L Turbo TCe 100 Petrol
engines.character: The accessible turbo: a three-cylinder that gives the Duster easy everyday pace with a 6-speed manual, and the sensible pick if the price of the 1.3 is a stretch. Manual only, and it tops out at the Techno trim

engines.name: 1.3L Turbo TCe 160 Petrol
engines.character: The muscle: 163 PS and 280 Nm make this the most powerful engine in the segment, strong and effortless on the highway. The 6-speed wet-clutch DCT is the relaxed, quick-shifting pick; the manual keeps it engaging

trims.name: Authentic
trims.positioning: The turbo-petrol base: eco-LED headlamps, the 7in digital driver display, all power windows and six airbags on 17in steel wheels. You go without the openR touchscreen, a camera, cruise and the sunroof, so it is the value entry more than the one to show off.

trims.name: Evolution
trims.positioning: The connectivity step, and a big one: the 25.65 cm openR link screen with wireless mirroring and six speakers, a rear camera, cruise control and 17in alloys. The first trim you can also have with the TCe 160 and its DCT.

trims.name: Techno
trims.positioning: The one most buyers will covet: full LED headlamps, the electric panoramic sunroof, a powered tailgate, connected services and automatic dual-zone AC arrive together.

trims.name: Techno+
trims.positioning: The tech step: the 26.03 cm digital cluster, blind-spot warning, front and side parking assist, hill descent control and 18in diamond-cut alloys. Sold only on the TCe 160.

trims.name: Iconic
trims.positioning: The flagship: 6-way electric ventilated front seats, leatherette, 48-colour ambient lighting and the full 17-function ADAS suite with adaptive cruise and the 360 camera.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: The full 17-function ADAS suite, with adaptive cruise, autonomous emergency braking and lane keep, is exclusive to the top Iconic (on either gearbox). Techno+ adds blind-spot warning and parking assist but not the driving-assist suite; the trims below have neither.

engines.name: 1.0L TSI Petrol
engines.character: A keen three-cylinder turbo that suits town and highway alike, and the only route to a manual. The new 8-speed automatic is the relaxed pick and costs you very little economy against the manual

engines.name: 1.5L TSI Petrol
engines.character: The enthusiast's engine: 150 PS with cylinder deactivation that runs it as a twin when cruising, DSG only, and it brings disc brakes on all four wheels

trims.name: Comfortline
trims.positioning: An honest floor: 6 airbags, auto AC, rear AC vents, a rear wiper and wired CarPlay all standard. You give up the camera, sunroof, alloys and cruise control, and the 7in screen is the smaller unit.

trims.name: Highline
trims.positioning: The tech step, and a big one: 10.1in screen with wireless CarPlay, rear camera, front sensors, wireless charging, 16in alloys and the split-folding rear seat in a single move. Cruise control and paddle shifters need the automatic here.

trims.name: Highline Plus
trims.positioning: The comfort step: electric sunroof, 8in digital cockpit, keyless entry, auto headlamps, rain-sensing wipers and auto-dimming mirror arrive together. Cruise still needs the automatic.

trims.name: GT Line
trims.positioning: The Sport line's entry: Highline Plus equipment in black GT dress with 17in black alloys as the one hardware change. Laser red ambient lighting and alu pedals set the tone; you pay about Rs 30,000 over Highline Plus for the look and the wheels.

trims.name: Topline
trims.positioning: The 1.0's flagship: panoramic sunroof, ventilated electric front seats, 10.25in cockpit, subwoofer audio, leatherette and the connected suite with SOS calling. Also the first trim with cruise control on the manual.

trims.name: GT Plus Chrome
trims.positioning: The 150 PS flagship: Topline's full kit on the 1.5 TSI DSG, with disc brakes on all four wheels and GT details in chrome. The GT Plus Sport sells the same kit in black trim for Rs 30,000 more.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Taigun offers any ADAS tier; the safety case is 6 standard airbags, the full stability suite and VW's 5-star Global NCAP claim.

engines.name: 1.0L TSI Petrol
engines.character: A keen three-cylinder turbo that punches above its size and returns the range's best economy with the manual. The 6-speed torque converter automatic is the relaxed choice, and the thirstiest of the three

engines.name: 1.5L TSI Petrol
engines.character: The enthusiast's engine: 150 PS with cylinder deactivation for cruising economy, DSG only, and certified thriftier than the 1.0 automatic despite the extra power

trims.name: Comfortline
trims.positioning: A bare but safe floor: 6 airbags, tyre deflation warning and 8 speakers even here, with wired CarPlay on a 7in screen. You give up auto AC, rear AC vents, the centre armrest, camera and alloys. MT only.

trims.name: Highline
trims.positioning: The big step, and most of the car arrives in it: 10.1in screen with wireless CarPlay, rear camera, cruise on both gearboxes, alloys, wireless charging, rear AC vents and the split rear seat. AC stays manual.

trims.name: Highline Plus
trims.positioning: The comfort step: Climatronic auto AC at last, plus the electric sunroof, 8in digital cockpit, keyless entry, auto headlamps, rain-sensing wipers and auto-dimming mirror, all for about Rs 40,000 over Highline.

trims.name: Topline
trims.positioning: The comfort flagship of the 1.0: segment-first ventilated electric front seats, leatherette, subwoofer-backed audio and the connected suite with SOS calling as standard.

trims.name: GT Plus
trims.positioning: The 150 PS flagship: Topline's full kit on the 1.5 TSI Evo DSG with GT chrome details, laser red ambient lighting and red front calipers. The GT Plus Sport sells the same kit in black trim for Rs 35,000 more.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Virtus offers any ADAS tier; the safety case is 6 standard airbags, the full stability suite and a 5-star Global NCAP rating for adult and child occupants.

engines.name: 2.0 TSI EVO Petrol 4MOTION
engines.officialEfficiencyBasis: Manufacturer figure, test cycle not stated
engines.character: A muscular 2.0 turbo-petrol that suits this SUV's quietly rapid character: instant DSG shifts, 4MOTION grip in any weather, and DCC Pro dampers that let it waft or hustle on demand. Refined pace rather than drama

trims.name: R-Line
trims.positioning: One fully loaded spec: 204 PS, 4MOTION grip, DCC Pro adaptive dampers, 21 ADAS functions and a 15in screen. Just know its European priorities: the seats massage and heat you but adjust manually and never ventilate, and there is no 360 camera or electric tailgate at Rs 47 lakh.

engines.name: 2.0 TSI EVO Petrol 4MOTION
engines.character: The 204 PS 2.0 turbo-petrol moves this three-row SUV with unstressed, quiet ease, and 4MOTION keeps it planted whatever the surface. Petrol-only where rivals offer diesel, so expect refinement over range between fill-ups

trims.name: Life
trims.positioning: The 5-seat value take: the same 204 PS 4MOTION drivetrain, all 14 ADAS functions, ventilated massaging seats, panoramic sunroof and a huge 885-litre boot for Rs 5.75 lakh less. You give up the third row, the Matrix LEDs, the head-up display, the 360 camera and the Harman Kardon.

trims.name: R-Line
trims.positioning: The 7-seat flagship: a usable third row plus IQ.LIGHT Matrix LEDs, an AR head-up display, 360 camera, 15in screen and 700W Harman Kardon in sportier dress. The step buys tech and seats; the drivetrain is identical.

engines.name: 1.0L TSI Petrol
engines.character: A three-cylinder turbo petrol with more shove than the sub-4m norm: eager in the midrange, relaxed on the highway, with the Tiptronic automatic the easygoing pick

trims.name: Classic
trims.positioning: Six airbags, ESC and roof rails even at the floor price, but no touchscreen at all: the audio is wiring and tweeters awaiting a radio. MT only.

trims.name: Classic+
trims.positioning: One rung up buys the electric sunroof, cruise, rain-sensing wipers and an auto-dimming mirror. Still screenless, but the automatic starts here.

trims.name: Signature
trims.positioning: The tech floor: the first touchscreen with wired CarPlay, TPMS, alloys, a cooled glovebox and the rear wiper arrive together.

trims.name: Signature+
trims.positioning: The step worth studying: 10.1in screen with wireless CarPlay, the digital cockpit, auto AC, rear camera and keyless entry in one move.

trims.name: Sportline
trims.positioning: The sportier cosmetic pick: Signature+'s tech plus LED projector headlamps and fogs, 17in black alloys and Sportline-branded leatherette, without Prestige's ventilated seats.

trims.name: Prestige
trims.positioning: The comfort trim: ventilated leatherette seats, wireless charging, ambient lighting, LED projector headlamps and 17in alloys.

trims.name: Prestige+
trims.positioning: The flagship adds 6-way electric adjustment for both front seats to the full Prestige kit, for a small step in price.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Kylaq offers any ADAS tier; its safety case is six standard airbags, the full stability suite and a 5-star BNCAP rating.

engines.name: 1.0 TSI Petrol
engines.character: A punchy three-cylinder turbo that suits both town and highway, and the only route to a manual. The new 8-speed torque converter is the relaxed pick and out-scores the manual's economy figure barely at all

engines.name: 1.5 TSI Petrol
engines.character: The enthusiast's engine: 150 PS with cylinder deactivation that runs it as a twin when cruising, DSG only, and it brings disc brakes on all four wheels

trims.name: Classic+
trims.positioning: An unusually complete base: 6 airbags, alloys, an electric sunroof, auto AC, rain-sensing wipers and an auto-dimming mirror all standard. Cruise control and LED fogs need the automatic, and there is no camera, TPMS or USB-C at this rung.

trims.name: Signature
trims.positioning: The tech step, and a big one: 10.1in screen with wireless CarPlay and an AI assistant, digital cluster, TPMS, rear camera, front sensors, keyless entry, wireless charging and 17in alloys in a single move.

trims.name: Sportline
trims.positioning: Signature's exact kit in sportier dress: black 17in alloys, gloss black trim, aluminium pedals and Sportline badging for Rs 15,000 more. The look is the whole upgrade.

trims.name: Prestige
trims.positioning: The comfort flagship: panoramic sunroof, ventilated powered front seats, the segment-first rear seat massager, 10.25in cluster, subwoofer-backed audio and beige leatherette. Also the only trim sold with all three powertrains.

trims.name: Monte Carlo
trims.positioning: Prestige's full kit in red-and-black motorsport dress, with red calipers on the 1.5 and a red-themed cockpit. Automatic only, and you pay Rs 20-30,000 over Prestige for the styling.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Kushaq offers ADAS at any price; the safety case rests on 6 standard airbags and a 5-star Global NCAP result instead.

engines.name: 1.0L TSI Petrol
engines.character: A three-cylinder turbo petrol that punches above its size: keen in the midrange and easy on fuel, with the torque-converter automatic the relaxed choice

engines.name: 1.5L TSI Petrol
engines.character: The enthusiast's engine: 150 PS with cylinder deactivation for cruising economy, quick off the line and long-legged, sold only with the fast-shifting 7-speed DSG

trims.name: Classic
trims.positioning: A solid floor: six airbags, TPMS and a 7in screen with wired CarPlay even here, but manual AC, 15in steels and no sunroof. MT only.

trims.name: Signature
trims.positioning: The big step: sunroof, 10in screen with wireless CarPlay, auto AC, rear camera, cruise, alloys and wireless charging arrive together.

trims.name: Prestige
trims.positioning: The comfort flagship: ventilated leatherette seats with 6-way electric adjustment, the digital cockpit, auto headlamps and a subwoofer-backed sound system. Also the only door to the 150 PS 1.5 TSI.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Slavia offers any ADAS tier; its safety case is six standard airbags, the full stability suite and a 5-star Global NCAP rating.

engines.name: 2.0 TSI Petrol 4x4
engines.character: A muscular 2.0 turbo-petrol that moves this big 4x4 with real urgency, and the DSG suits it: refined and effortless rather than thrilling, with all-weather sure-footedness the segment's front-drivers lack

trims.name: Lounge
trims.positioning: The 5-seat value take: the same 204 PS 4x4 drivetrain, 9 airbags, panoramic sunroof, 3-zone climate and a huge 786-litre boot for Rs 8 lakh less. You give up the third row, the ADAS suite, the 360 camera and the Canton audio.

trims.name: Sportline
trims.positioning: The sporty 7-seater, and since 2026 the sensible tech buy: the full ADAS suite, Matrix LEDs, 360 camera, 12.9in screen and Canton audio in black-on-black dress, Rs 2 lakh below the L&K.

trims.name: Selection L&K
trims.positioning: The luxury flagship: Cognac leather and Ergo front seats with pneumatic massage, ventilation and heating on top of Sportline's full tech and ADAS kit. The Rs 2 lakh step buys comfort, not capability.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: The 2026 update brought ADAS to the Kodiaq, but only on Sportline and Selection L&K: adaptive cruise, Front Assist with braking, Lane Assist, Side Assist, Rear Traffic Alert and Exit Warning. The Lounge goes without it.

engines.name: 1.5L Turbo Petrol
engines.character: A relaxed, quiet 1.5 turbo that suits the Hector's easygoing nature; the CVT is the smoother match for town, the 6-speed manual the cheaper one

trims.name: Style
trims.positioning: The price-fighter: 6 airbags, all-disc brakes and a full-size body for compact-SUV money. No touchscreen, no sunroof, no cruise, and halogen lamps tell you how.

trims.name: Select Pro
trims.positioning: The step that makes it a Hector: 14in screen with wireless CarPlay, dual-pane panoramic sunroof, LED projectors, alloys, cruise and a wireless charger in one move. No connected tech yet.

trims.name: Smart Pro
trims.positioning: The connected step: full i-Smart with E-Call, TPMS, front sensors, 18in alloys and leatherette. Take the CVT and it adds an electronic parking brake and drive modes.

trims.name: Sharp Pro
trims.positioning: The comfort step: ventilated powered front seats, auto headlamps and wipers, Infinity by Harman audio, ambient lighting and auto AC. Everything but the driver aids.

trims.name: Savvy Pro
trims.positioning: The flagship, CVT only: the range's only Level 2 ADAS with adaptive cruise, a 360 camera with wheel view, powered tailgate and an air purifier.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: Level 2 ADAS with adaptive cruise exists only on the top Savvy Pro, which is CVT-only. Every other trim has ordinary cruise control at most, and the base Style has none.
priorityNotes.panoramic-sunroof: The dual-pane panoramic sunroof is standard from Select Pro up. Only the base Style goes without it.

engines.name: 1.5L Turbo Petrol
engines.character: The Hector's relaxed 1.5 turbo pulling a heavier seven-seat cabin: unstressed rather than quick, and the CVT is the easier companion when all three rows are full

trims.name: Sharp Pro
trims.positioning: The three-row entry point, and already nearly loaded: ventilated powered front seats, Infinity by Harman audio, auto lamps and wipers, plus a third row with its own AC control.

trims.name: Savvy Pro
trims.positioning: The flagship, CVT only: the family's only Level 2 ADAS with adaptive cruise, a 360 camera with wheel view, powered tailgate and an air purifier.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: Level 2 ADAS with adaptive cruise exists only on the top Savvy Pro, which is CVT-only. The Sharp Pro makes do with ordinary cruise control.
priorityNotes.panoramic-sunroof: Every Hector Plus has the dual-pane panoramic sunroof; both trims carry it.

engines.name: 69.2 kWh Electric
engines.character: The volume Tomahawk: a single 204 PS motor, a 517 km certified range and LFP chemistry MG markets on safety as much as range

trims.name: Excite
trims.positioning: The price-fighter entry into the Tomahawk EV: 6 airbags, all-disc brakes, a reversing camera and 18in alloys, but no panoramic sunroof, no 360 camera and a smaller 12.8in screen.

trims.name: Exclusive
trims.positioning: The step most buyers should make: the 15.6in GrandView screen, 360 camera, panoramic sunroof, ventilated front seats and wireless charging arrive together.

trims.name: Essence (5-seater)
trims.positioning: The two-row top trim: Level 2 ADAS, the 10-speaker Infinity system, seat memory and Vehicle-to-Home charging, without a third row to lose to the extra kit.

trims.name: Essence (7-seater)
trims.positioning: The full-house three-row Tomahawk EV: everything the 5-seater Essence has, plus the third row and its own AC vents.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: Level 2 ADAS is fitted only to the top Essence trim, in both its seat counts; Excite and Exclusive go without it. The core safety kit (6 airbags, ESC, all-disc brakes, ISOFIX, TPMS) is standard from the base Excite up.

engines.name: 1.5L DHT Plug-in Hybrid
engines.character: The plug-in Tomahawk: a 1.5L Atkinson petrol and a 20.5 kWh pack through a Dedicated Hybrid Transmission, claimed for 115 km on electric alone and over 1,100 km combined

trims.name: Exclusive
trims.positioning: Most of what the Tomahawk PHEV offers in one variant: panoramic sunroof, ventilated front seats, 360 camera and drive modes, without Level 2 ADAS, rear sunshades or an auto-dimming mirror.

trims.name: Essence
trims.positioning: The full-house Tomahawk PHEV: Level 2 ADAS with adaptive cruise, rear sunshades, an auto-dimming mirror and the 10-speaker Infinity system on top of everything Exclusive has.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: Level 2 ADAS is fitted only to the top Essence trim; the Exclusive goes without it, though it carries the rest of the safety kit (6 airbags, ESC, EPB, all-disc brakes, TPMS, front and rear parking sensors, a 360 camera).

engines.name: 1.5L VTi-TECH Petrol
engines.character: An unstressed naturally aspirated petrol that suits town running; pick it for smoothness rather than pace, with the CVT the relaxed choice

trims.name: Sprint
trims.positioning: The full-size screen and auto AC from the base trim, but 2 airbags, steel wheels and no CarPlay.

trims.name: Shine
trims.positioning: The panoramic sunroof, cruise, alloys and a reversing camera arrive one rung up, still on 2 airbags.

trims.name: Select
trims.positioning: The safety and tech step: 6 airbags, TPMS, wireless CarPlay, connected car tech and the digital cluster.

trims.name: Sharp Pro
trims.positioning: The comfort trim: ventilated seats, powered driver seat, 360 camera and rain-sensing wipers.

trims.name: Savvy Pro
trims.positioning: The only Astor with ADAS: 14 Level-2 functions including adaptive cruise and blind spot detection. CVT only.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: ADAS is only on the top Savvy Pro trim, a 14-function Level 2 suite; no other Astor offers any ADAS tier.

engines.name: 50.3 kWh Electric
engines.officialEfficiencyBasis: Certified at government-affiliated test agencies (cycle not named by MG)
engines.character: Brisk and quiet: 280 Nm from a standstill, 0-100 in 8.5 s and a claimed 461 km make it the long-legged, quick one

trims.name: Executive
trims.positioning: The full 461 km powertrain with 6 airbags, EPB and connected tech from the base trim; no sunroof and wired CarPlay only.

trims.name: Excite Pro
trims.positioning: The dual-pane panoramic roof, wireless CarPlay and JBL speakers arrive one rung up.

trims.name: Exclusive Plus
trims.positioning: The comfort trim: 360 camera, blind spot kit, leatherette, powered driver seat and wireless charging.

trims.name: Essence
trims.positioning: The only ZS EV with ADAS: MG's 17-function Level 2 suite with adaptive cruise and traffic jam assist.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: The 17-function Level 2 ADAS suite is only on the top Essence trim; Exclusive Plus gets blind spot detection, lane change assist and rear cross traffic alert but no ADAS package.

engines.name: 17.3 kWh Electric
engines.character: A tiny rear-motor city car that turns in 4.2 metres: made for tight streets and short hops, with overnight 3.3 kW charging as the only option

engines.name: 17.4 kWh Electric Fast Charge
engines.character: The same city runabout but with 7.4 kW AC charging, cutting a full charge from 7 hours to 3.5. There is still no DC port, by design

trims.name: Executive
trims.positioning: The cheapest way into the Comet: digital cluster, two speakers and manual AC, but no touchscreen, no camera, and slow 3.3 kW charging only.

trims.name: Excite
trims.positioning: The tech step most buyers want: twin 10.25in screens, wireless CarPlay, LED lamps and connected i-Smart with eCall in one move.

trims.name: Exclusive
trims.positioning: The full Comet, and the only trim with the full safety kit: ESC, rear disc brakes, an electronic parking brake, a reverse camera and leatherette seats.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: The Comet EV has no ADAS of any level, and even ESC only arrives on the top Exclusive trim.

engines.name: 38 kWh Electric
engines.character: The city-and-suburbs Windsor: the same 136 PS motor and lounge-like cabin with a certified 332 km, at its best where charging is routine rather than rare

engines.name: 52.9 kWh Electric
engines.character: The Pro battery: a certified 449 km that turns the Windsor from a city car into a genuine intercity EV, with 60 kW DC charging for the highway stops

trims.name: Excite
trims.positioning: A strong base: 6 airbags, all-disc brakes, EPB with auto hold, auto AC, cruise and a 10.1in screen. But no camera of any kind, no rear defogger and no connected tech.

trims.name: Exclusive
trims.positioning: The step most buyers should make: the 15.6in screen, 360 camera, connected i-Smart with eCall, powered driver seat, alloys and wireless charger arrive in one move.

trims.name: Essence
trims.positioning: The comfort crown of the 38 kWh car: fixed glass roof, ventilated front seats, 256-colour ambient light and the 9-speaker Infinity system.

trims.name: Exclusive Pro
trims.positioning: The 52.9 kWh battery with Exclusive kit plus Infinity audio: 449 km certified, but you give up the Essence's glass roof, ventilated seats and ambient lighting.

trims.name: Essence Pro
trims.positioning: The full house: the 449 km battery, the only trim with Level 2 ADAS, plus a powered tailgate and V2L on top of everything the Essence has.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: Level 2 ADAS is fitted only to the top Essence Pro; every other Windsor, including the other 52.9 kWh car, goes without it. The core safety kit (6 airbags, ESC, all-disc brakes) is standard everywhere.

engines.name: 2.0L Twin-Turbo Diesel
engines.character: Big, unstressed twin-turbo torque through a smooth 8-speed auto: the rear-drive Majestor is the highway cruiser, and nothing about it asks to be hurried

engines.name: 2.0L Twin-Turbo Diesel Select 4x4
engines.character: The same engine with MG's Select 4x4: low range, 10 terrain modes, front, centre and rear differential locks, M-Crawl and 810 mm of wading. Pick it for genuinely hard ground, not for the badge

trims.name: Savvy
trims.positioning: The only trim, and it wants for almost nothing: massage and ventilation up front, JBL Studio 12, 3-zone climate, Level 2 ADAS and a 360 camera on every variant. Your only real choices are 4x2 or 4x4, and bench or captain seats.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: Level 2 ADAS with adaptive cruise is standard on every Majestor, 4x2 included. No variant goes without it.
priorityNotes.panoramic-sunroof: The Galaxy View panoramic roof is standard on every variant.

engines.name: 77 kWh Dual Motor AWD Electric
engines.character: MG's 510 PS dual-motor flagship: 0-100 in a claimed 3.2 seconds, AWD grip with a rear bias, and a claimed 580 km when you drive it gently

trims.name: GT
trims.positioning: The only spec MG sells, so nothing is optional: 510 PS, scissor doors, Brembo brakes, the triple-screen cockpit and a roof that drops in ten seconds.

engines.name: 90 kWh Single Motor Electric
engines.character: Smooth, near silent and tuned for the chauffeur driven: 245 PS, a 90 kWh pack and a claimed 548 km of unhurried calm

trims.name: Presidential Limo
trims.positioning: The one real spec: 16-way massage Presidential seats with powered ottomans, 3-zone climate, 13 JBL speakers and electric sliding doors. Nothing is held back for a higher trim.

engines.name: 1.2L i-VTEC Petrol
engines.character: The same easy-going 90 PS i-VTEC in the older body: relaxed, frugal and proven over years on the road

trims.name: S
trims.positioning: The only rung: Honda's proven basics at a runout price, but a previous-era spec with 2 airbags, no ESC and no touchscreen.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Amaze 2nd Gen variant offers ADAS, ESC or more than 2 airbags; the safety case is ABS, ISOFIX and rear parking sensors.

engines.name: 1.2L i-VTEC Petrol
engines.character: Smooth, rev-happy i-VTEC that is light on fuel; the CVT is actually the thriftier one here

trims.name: V
trims.positioning: A generous base: 6 airbags, ESC and the same 8-inch wireless CarPlay screen as the top car, on steel wheels with manual AC.

trims.name: VX
trims.positioning: The comfort step: alloys, rear camera with LaneWatch, auto climate, smart key, wireless charger and connected tech.

trims.name: ZX
trims.positioning: The only rung with Honda Sensing: adaptive cruise, lane keeping and collision mitigation on either gearbox.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: Honda Sensing is exclusive to the top ZX trim, on both gearboxes; V and VX offer no ADAS at any price.

engines.name: 1.5L i-VTEC Petrol
engines.character: Free-revving and smooth in the classic Honda way, with more top-end power than the segment's usual 1.5s. Also the only route to a manual gearbox

engines.name: 1.5L e:HEV Strong Hybrid
engines.torqueNote: 253 Nm is the electric motor's figure; the Atkinson-cycle petrol engine adds 131 Nm of its own
engines.character: Two motors do most of the town running with the engine joining at speed: near-silent, effortless progress and economy no pure petrol sedan matches

trims.name: SV
trims.positioning: An unusually complete base: 8in screen, rear camera, six airbags and auto AC. But no Honda Sensing, and no cruise control at any price on this trim.

trims.name: V
trims.positioning: The step worth making: Honda Sensing with adaptive cruise on manual and CVT alike, wireless CarPlay, connected tech and alloys in one move.

trims.name: ZX
trims.positioning: The comfort step: sunroof, 10.1in screen with eight speakers, leather-mix seats, rain-sensing wipers and the LaneWatch blind-spot camera.

trims.name: ZX+
trims.positioning: The petrol flagship: 360 camera, ventilated front seats, a 7in digital cluster and auto-folding mirrors over the ZX.

trims.name: ZX+ e:HEV
trims.positioning: The hybrid crown: the 27.26 km/l strong hybrid adds all-disc brakes, an electronic parking brake with auto hold and low-speed follow to the full ZX+ kit.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: Honda Sensing arrives one step up from the base: V, ZX and ZX+ carry it on manual and CVT alike, and the e:HEV adds low-speed follow. The base SV goes without it, and without any cruise control.

engines.name: 1.5L i-VTEC Petrol
engines.character: The City's free-revving 1.5 carried up into an SUV: smooth and relaxed rather than rapid, and happiest worked through the CVT in town

trims.name: SV
trims.positioning: A bare-bones price leader: six airbags and LED projectors, but no touchscreen, no speakers, no rear camera and no rear defogger. Most buyers should start one step up.

trims.name: V
trims.positioning: Where the Elevate properly begins: 8in screen with wireless CarPlay, rear camera, four speakers and connected tech in one step.

trims.name: VX
trims.positioning: The value peak: sunroof, 17in alloys, LED fogs, wireless charger, auto-folding mirrors and the LaneWatch camera arrive together.

trims.name: ZX
trims.positioning: The only trim with Honda Sensing: adaptive cruise and lane keeping on either gearbox, plus the 10.25in screen, leatherette and eight speakers.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: Honda Sensing is reserved for the top ZX, on both gearboxes. SV, V and VX offer no driver assistance, and no cruise control of any kind.

engines.name: 2.0L e:HEV Strong Hybrid
engines.character: Two motors handle most town driving with the 2.0 joining in at speed: hushed, unhurried progress and the only hybrid option Honda sells this large in India

trims.name: e:HEV
trims.positioning: The only way to buy a ZR-V: Honda's full Level 2 Sensing suite, a 12-speaker Bose system and leatherette on every car sold here. What it does not offer, at any price, is a sunroof or ventilated seats, a real gap against rivals in this bracket.

engines.name: 2.0L 4-cylinder Petrol
engines.character: A 2.0-litre 4-cylinder petrol, 421 PS and 500 Nm; 0 to 100 km/h in 3.9 seconds by Mercedes' figure

trims.name: Aero Track Edition

trims.name: xDrive40i M Sport Pro

trims.name: xDrive30d M Sport Pro
trims.positioning: Rs 2 lakh more than the xDrive40i M Sport Pro buys the 3.0-litre diesel (286 PS), with the same equipment otherwise. You give up off-road drive modes.

trims.name: xDrive
trims.positioning: The only X6 M60i BMW sells here: the 4.4-litre petrol (530 PS), with a 360 camera, a panoramic glass roof, Harman Kardon sound and ventilated front seats as standard.

engines.name: 3.0L 6-cylinder Diesel

engines.name: 3.0L 6-cylinder Petrol
engines.character: A 3.0-litre 6-cylinder turbo petrol, 381 PS and 520 Nm, driving all four wheels; 0 to 100 km/h in 5.8 seconds by BMW's figure

trims.name: xDrive40d DPE
trims.positioning: Where the X7 starts: the 3.0-litre diesel (340 PS), with a 360 camera, a panoramic glass roof, Harman Kardon sound and ventilated front seats as standard.

trims.name: xDrive40i M Sport
trims.positioning: Rs 2.7 lakh more than the xDrive40d DPE buys the 3.0-litre petrol (381 PS), and adds Bowers & Wilkins sound with 20 speakers, 21-inch wheels and individual rear seats.

trims.name: xDrive40d M Sport
trims.positioning: Rs 3.7 lakh more than the xDrive40i M Sport buys the 3.0-litre diesel (340 PS), with the same equipment otherwise.

engines.name: 2.0L 4-cylinder Petrol Mild Hybrid
engines.character: A 2.0-litre 4-cylinder turbo petrol with a mild-hybrid starter-generator, 204 PS and 320 Nm, driving the front wheels; 0 to 100 km/h in 7.1 seconds by Audi's figure

trims.name: Premium
trims.positioning: Where the A4 starts: the 2.0-litre petrol mild hybrid (204 PS), with a glass sunroof as standard.

trims.name: Premium Plus
trims.positioning: Rs 4.97 lakh more than the Premium adds Audi's fully digital virtual cockpit and 8 airbags instead of 6.

trims.name: Technology
