engines.name: 2.0L 4-cylinder Petrol Mild Hybrid
engines.character: A 2.0-litre 4-cylinder turbo petrol with a mild-hybrid starter-generator, 265 PS and 370 Nm, driving the front wheels; 0 to 100 km/h in 6.7 seconds by Audi's figure

trims.name: Premium Plus
trims.positioning: Where the A6 starts: the 2.0-litre petrol mild hybrid (265 PS), with a panoramic glass roof as standard.

trims.name: Technology
trims.positioning: Rs 6.85 lakh more than the Premium Plus adds Bang & Olufsen sound with 16 speakers, Matrix LED headlamps, 19-inch wheels, a 360 camera and an air ionizer.

engines.name: 2.0L 4-cylinder Petrol Mild Hybrid
engines.character: A 2.0-litre 4-cylinder turbo petrol with a mild-hybrid starter-generator, 265 PS and 370 Nm, driving all four wheels through quattro; 0 to 100 km/h in 6.1 seconds by Audi's figure

trims.name: Premium Plus
trims.positioning: Where the Q5 starts: the 2.0-litre petrol mild hybrid (265 PS), with a panoramic glass roof as standard.

trims.name: Technology
trims.positioning: Rs 5.18 lakh more than the Premium Plus adds Bang & Olufsen sound with 19 speakers, a 360 camera, a memory driver's seat and adaptive suspension.

engines.name: 3.0L V6 Petrol Mild Hybrid
engines.character: A 3.0-litre V6 turbo petrol with a mild-hybrid starter-generator, 340 PS and 500 Nm, driving all four wheels through quattro; 0 to 100 km/h in 5.6 seconds by Audi's figure

trims.name: Premium Plus
trims.positioning: Where the Q7 starts: the 3.0-litre V6 petrol mild hybrid (340 PS), with a panoramic glass roof and adaptive suspension as standard.

trims.name: Technology
trims.positioning: Rs 8.98 lakh more than the Premium Plus adds Bang & Olufsen sound with 19 speakers, Matrix LED headlamps, 20-inch wheels, a 360 camera and an air ionizer.

engines.name: 3.0L V6 Petrol Mild Hybrid
engines.character: A 3.0-litre V6 turbo petrol with a mild-hybrid starter-generator, 340 PS and 500 Nm, driving all four wheels through quattro; 0 to 100 km/h in 5.6 seconds by Audi's figure

trims.name: 55 TFSI quattro
trims.positioning: The only Q8 Audi sells here: the 3.0-litre V6 petrol mild hybrid (340 PS), with a 360 camera, a panoramic glass roof, Matrix LED headlamps and Bang & Olufsen sound as standard.

engines.name: 4.0L V8 Petrol
engines.character: A 4.0-litre V8 turbo petrol, 507 PS and 770 Nm, driving all four wheels through quattro; 0 to 100 km/h in 4.1 seconds by Audi's figure

trims.name: TFSI quattro
trims.positioning: The only SQ8 Audi sells here: the 4.0-litre V8 petrol (507 PS), with a 360 camera, a panoramic glass roof, Matrix LED headlamps and Bang & Olufsen sound as standard.

engines.name: 4.0L V8 Petrol Mild Hybrid
engines.character: A 4.0-litre V8 turbo petrol with a mild-hybrid starter-generator, 640 PS and 850 Nm, driving all four wheels through quattro; 0 to 100 km/h in 3.6 seconds by Audi's figure

trims.name: Performance
trims.positioning: The only RS Q8 Audi sells here: the 4.0-litre V8 petrol mild hybrid (640 PS), with a 360 camera, Matrix LED headlamps, Bang & Olufsen sound and ventilated front seats as standard.

engines.name: 2.5L Hybrid
engines.torqueNote: 238 Nm is the petrol engine's figure; the front motor adds 270 Nm and the rear 121 Nm, and Lexus publishes no combined torque
engines.character: Lexus's self-charging 2.5-litre hybrid with a second motor on the rear axle for all-wheel drive: 176 kW (239 PS) combined, 0 to 100 km/h in 7.7 seconds by Lexus's figure, and 20.26 km/l on Lexus's own sheet

trims.name: Exquisite
trims.positioning: Where the NX starts: the same 2.5-litre all-wheel-drive hybrid as every NX, a panoramic roof, ventilated front seats, a head-up display and Lexus's full safety suite. It skips the 360 camera and the wireless charger.

trims.name: Overtrail
trims.positioning: The outdoorsy NX: 18-inch wheels with taller tyres, black trim, adaptive dampers, a 360 camera and 17-speaker Mark Levinson sound, for Rs 3.86 lakh over the Exquisite.

trims.name: Luxury
trims.positioning: The comfort pick: the Overtrail's 360 camera, wireless charger and Mark Levinson sound on 20-inch wheels and leather, without the adaptive dampers.

trims.name: F SPORT
trims.positioning: The top NX: everything the Luxury has, plus adaptive dampers, sport seats and Sport S and S+ drive modes, for Rs 2.18 lakh more.

engines.name: 2.5L Hybrid
engines.torqueNote: 238 Nm is the petrol engine's figure; the front motor adds 270 Nm and the rear 121 Nm, and Lexus publishes no combined torque
engines.character: Lexus's self-charging 2.5-litre hybrid with a rear motor for all-wheel drive: 181 kW (246 PS) combined and 0 to 100 km/h in 7.9 seconds by Lexus's figure

trims.name: Exquisite
trims.positioning: The RX 350h as Lexus India sells it: the 2.5-litre all-wheel-drive hybrid, 21-inch wheels, a panoramic roof, heated and ventilated seats front and rear, a 360 camera and a head-up display, with Lexus's own audio.

trims.name: Exquisite with Mark Levinson
trims.positioning: The same RX 350h with the 21-speaker Mark Levinson system in place of Lexus's own audio, for Rs 3.43 lakh more. Nothing else changes.

engines.name: 2.4L Turbo Hybrid
engines.torqueNote: 460 Nm is the turbo petrol engine's figure; the front motor adds 292 Nm and the rear 168.5 Nm, and Lexus publishes no combined torque
engines.character: A 2.4-litre turbo petrol hybrid with Lexus's DIRECT4 all-wheel drive and rear-wheel steering: 273 kW (371 PS) combined and 0 to 100 km/h in 6.2 seconds by Lexus's figure, the quickest RX

trims.name: F SPORT+
trims.positioning: The performance RX: a 2.4-litre turbo hybrid making 371 PS through DIRECT4 all-wheel drive, rear-wheel steering, F SPORT styling and 21-inch matte black wheels. Rs 20.11 lakh over the RX 350h.

engines.name: 3.3L V6 Twin-Turbo Diesel
engines.character: A 3.3-litre twin-turbo V6 diesel with 227 kW (309 PS) and 700 Nm from 1,600 rpm, on a body-on-frame chassis with height-adjustable suspension: built to carry five in comfort and still go properly off road

trims.name: Urban
trims.positioning: The LX for the road: the 3.3-litre twin-turbo V6 diesel, 22-inch forged wheels, height-adjustable air suspension, 25-speaker Mark Levinson sound, rear-seat screens and ventilated seats front and rear.

trims.name: Overtrail
trims.positioning: The LX built for rough ground: front and rear differential locks and 18-inch wheels with tall tyres, plus black exterior trim and the Moon Desert paint, for Rs 11.66 lakh more.

engines.name: 2.5L Hybrid
engines.torqueNote: 139 kW and 237 Nm are the petrol engine's figures; Lexus India adds a 119.1 kW electric motor and publishes no combined output
engines.character: Lexus's self-charging 2.5-litre hybrid driving the front wheels: a 139 kW petrol engine and a 119.1 kW electric motor that lets the ES creep and cruise on electric power alone, and it never needs a plug

trims.name: Exquisite
trims.positioning: Where the new ES starts: the 2.5-litre self-charging hybrid, 19-inch wheels, a sunroof, a 14-inch screen, radar cruise and lane tracing. It does without the 360 camera, ventilated seats and head-up display.

trims.name: Luxury
trims.positioning: Rs 5.70 lakh more adds the comfort the Exquisite leaves out: ventilated and heated front seats, a 360 camera, a head-up display, a wireless charger, 17-speaker Mark Levinson sound and a nanoe X air purifier.

engines.name: Dual Motor AWD
engines.character: Two motors and all-wheel drive, 252 kW (343 PS) and 438 Nm, on a 74.68 kWh battery: 0 to 100 km/h in 5.5 seconds and 580 km of range by Lexus's figures, and 10 to 80 percent in 28 minutes on a 150 kW charger

trims.name: Luxury
trims.positioning: The electric ES, one fully loaded variant: two motors and all-wheel drive, 580 km of claimed range, 21-inch wheels, adaptive dampers, semi-aniline leather, a 360 camera, a head-up display and 17-speaker Mark Levinson sound.

engines.name: 2.5L Hybrid
engines.torqueNote: 239 Nm is the petrol engine's figure; the front motor adds 270 Nm and the rear 121 Nm, and Lexus publishes no combined torque
engines.character: Lexus's self-charging 2.5-litre hybrid with E-Four all-wheel drive, 182 kW (247 PS) combined: it moves this five-metre lounge in near silence and never needs a plug

trims.name: 7-Seater VIP
trims.positioning: The LM as a seven-seat lounge: two powered second-row seats with ottomans, a split third row, 21-speaker Mark Levinson sound and a ceiling-mounted rear screen, on the quiet 2.5-litre hybrid.

trims.name: 4-Seater Ultra Luxury
trims.positioning: The chauffeur's LM: four seats, a dimming privacy partition with a 48-inch rear screen, a refrigerator, massaging rear seats and 23-speaker Mark Levinson sound, for Rs 56.86 lakh more.

engines.name: 1.2L K-Series Dual Jet Petrol
engines.character: Light, frugal city engine with idle start-stop; happiest in town, worked hard on the highway

engines.name: 1.2L K-Series E-CNG
engines.character: The cheapest Glanza to run per km, trading some pep and boot space for it

trims.name: E
trims.positioning: Honest base: 6 airbags, auto AC and a rear defogger, but no screen and no speakers at all.

trims.name: S
trims.positioning: The sensible start: 7-inch touchscreen with CarPlay, four speakers, and the cheaper of the two CNG doors.

trims.name: G
trims.positioning: The value pick: LED projectors, alloys, rear camera and connected tech, and the CNG ladder tops out here.

trims.name: V
trims.positioning: The full hatch: 9-inch screen, 360 camera, head-up display and cruise control.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Glanza variant offers ADAS at any price; the safety case is 6 airbags, ESC and hill hold on every trim.

engines.name: 1.2L K-Series Dual Jet Petrol
engines.character: Easygoing and economical with idle start-stop; fine in town, worked hard on the highway

engines.name: 1.0L K-Series Turbo Smart Hybrid
engines.character: The one enthusiasts pick: punchier mid-range with mild-hybrid assist, and the only engine with a torque-converter automatic

engines.name: 1.2L K-Series E-CNG
engines.character: Cheapest per km to run, with the usual CNG trade of some power and boot space

trims.name: E
trims.positioning: The only door into CNG, and honestly equipped: 6 airbags, auto AC and a rear defogger, but no screen or speakers.

trims.name: S
trims.positioning: The sensible start: 7-inch screen with wireless CarPlay and four speakers.

trims.name: S+
trims.positioning: The looks step: LED lamps with twin DRLs, auto headlamps and alloys on the same 1.2 petrol.

trims.name: G
trims.positioning: Turbo-only from here: rear camera, wireless charger, connected tech and the proper 6-speed automatic option.

trims.name: V
trims.positioning: The full crossover kit: 9-inch screen, 360 camera, head-up display and cruise control.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Taisor variant offers ADAS at any price; the safety case is 6 airbags, ESC and hill hold on every trim.

engines.name: 1.5L K Series Neodrive Petrol
engines.character: Smooth and unstressed with seven aboard rather than quick; the 6-speed automatic with paddles is the easy family pick

engines.name: 1.5L K Series E-CNG
engines.torqueNote: 121.5 Nm in CNG mode; running on petrol the same engine makes 137.1 Nm
engines.character: The running-costs champion for the school run and the taxi shift, if you can live with the tank taking most of the boot

trims.name: E
trims.positioning: The price of entry: all six airbags, ESC and three usable rows are here, but there is no audio at all and the AC is manual. Worth it only if every rupee counts.

trims.name: S
trims.positioning: The family floor most buyers should start at: keyless entry, Bluetooth audio and powered folding mirrors, and it is the only trim sold as a CNG.

trims.name: G
trims.positioning: The sweet spot: the 7-inch screen with wireless CarPlay, auto AC, push start, rear camera and alloys land in one step, and the automatic opens up.

trims.name: V
trims.positioning: The top of a short ladder: cruise control, auto headlamps and TPMS over the G. A modest step, so weigh it against putting the money toward the automatic.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Rumion offers driver assistance at any price; the safety case is six airbags, ESC and ISOFIX standard from the base E.
priorityNotes.sunroof: No Rumion gets a sunroof, whichever trim you pick; the ladder climbs in tech and convenience, not glass.

engines.name: 1.5L K Series Neodrive Petrol
engines.character: Easygoing rather than quick, with a mild-hybrid assist in stop-start traffic; the relaxed choice if the hybrid premium is a stretch

engines.name: 1.5L K Series E-CNG
engines.torqueNote: 121.5 Nm in CNG mode; running on petrol the same engine makes 136 Nm
engines.character: Rock-bottom running costs with the usual CNG trades: a 5-speed manual only and a tank in the boot

engines.name: 1.5L TNGA Strong Hybrid e-Drive
engines.torqueNote: 141 Nm is the electric motor's figure; the petrol engine adds 122 Nm of its own
engines.character: Toyota's self-charging hybrid: silent electric running in town, never plugs in, and the economy champion of the range at a claimed 27.97 km/l

trims.name: E
trims.positioning: A true price leader: six airbags, all-disc brakes and auto AC are here, but no touchscreen, camera or TPMS. Most buyers should stretch one step up.

trims.name: S
trims.positioning: Where the Hyryder starts making sense: 7-inch screen with CarPlay, rear camera, cruise, TPMS and connected tech in one jump. The automatic adds an electronic parking brake.

trims.name: G(O)
trims.positioning: The value peak: panoramic sunroof, ventilated seats, the 9-inch screen with premium audio, LED projectors and wireless charging arrive together.

trims.name: V
trims.positioning: The petrol flagship: 360 camera, head-up display, powered driver's seat and leatherette over the G(O).

trims.name: S E-CNG
trims.positioning: The cheapest route to CNG running costs, with the S's screen, camera and cruise. Manual only, and the tank takes a bite of the boot.

trims.name: G E-CNG
trims.positioning: A CNG rarity: ventilated seats, the 9-inch screen and wireless charging with CNG running costs. You give up the panoramic sunroof and any automatic.

trims.name: S Hybrid
trims.positioning: The affordable door into the strong hybrid: S kit with drive modes and silent electric running in town, no plug ever needed.

trims.name: G(O) Hybrid
trims.positioning: The hybrid sweet spot: panoramic sunroof and ventilated seats with the 27.97 km/l drivetrain. The head-up display stays with the V.

trims.name: V Hybrid
trims.positioning: Everything the Hyryder offers in one car: 360 camera, head-up display, leatherette and the economy champion drivetrain.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Hyryder offers driver assistance at any price; the safety case is six airbags, ESC, all-disc brakes and TPMS instead.

engines.name: 61 kWh Electric
engines.character: Toyota's first ground-up EV for India: a durable LFP pack, a claimed 543 km, and the quiet instant shove of an electric motor in town

trims.name: E3
trims.positioning: The only trim priced so far, and it is the full house: 7 airbags, Level 2 ADAS, 360 camera, ventilated seats, JBL audio and the glass roof.

engines.name: 2.4L GD Turbo Diesel
engines.character: The unstressed workhorse: 343 Nm driving the rear wheels through a 5-speed manual, built for lakhs of kilometres rather than lap times

trims.name: GX
trims.positioning: The working base of the priced range: the 8in screen with CarPlay, 16in alloys and manual AC, with 3 airbags the honest catch.

trims.name: GX+
trims.positioning: The camera step: a reversing camera with built-in dash recorder, folding mirrors with welcome lamps, and smarter trim.

trims.name: VX
trims.positioning: Where the Crysta grows up: 7 airbags, auto LED projectors, climate control, cruise and a wireless charger in one jump.

trims.name: ZX
trims.positioning: The chauffeur spec: leather, powered driver seat, TPMS and 17in alloys, sold with the captain-seat layout only.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Innova Crysta variant offers ADAS at any level, and GX and GX+ carry 3 airbags against the 7 on VX and ZX.

engines.name: 2.0L TNGA Petrol
engines.character: The honest workhorse: smooth, unstressed and a lakh cheaper to buy, but it drinks noticeably more than the hybrid in town

engines.name: 2.0L TNGA Strong Hybrid
engines.torqueNote: 206 Nm is the electric motor's figure; the petrol engine adds 191 Nm of its own
engines.character: Toyota's self-charging hybrid: silent electric running in town and diesel-beating economy from a seven-seater, with no plug to think about

trims.name: G-SLF 7S
trims.positioning: The fleet special, and it says so: an 80 km/h speed limiter, no touchscreen and no rear camera. Built for taxi duty, not for your driveway.

trims.name: G-SLF 8S
trims.positioning: The same fleet spec with a bench for eight and one seat belt more. The 80 km/h limiter stays, so private buyers should look one step up.

trims.name: GX 7S
trims.positioning: Where the retail range really starts: no speed limiter, an 8in screen with CarPlay, rear camera, connected tech and captain seats.

trims.name: GX 8S
trims.positioning: The GX with a 60:40 bench when carrying eight matters more than lounging. Everything else carries over.

trims.name: GX(O) 8S
trims.positioning: The sensible petrol pick for big families: auto climate, 360 camera, front sensors and LED fogs on the eight-seat bench.

trims.name: GX(O) 7S
trims.positioning: The petrol range topper: the 10.1in screen with wireless CarPlay and a rear sunshade join the captain seats, for Rs 0.13 lakh over the bench.

trims.name: VX 7S
trims.positioning: The hybrid entry, and a big step: ventilated seats, cruise control, drive modes and the TFT cluster. Oddly, the screen drops back to 8in here.

trims.name: VX 8S
trims.positioning: The hybrid with a bench for eight: the same VX kit, one more seat, Rs 0.05 lakh more.

trims.name: VX(O) 7S
trims.positioning: The cheapest panoramic sunroof in the range, and the 10.1in screen with wireless CarPlay returns. The sweet spot if the ZX is a stretch.

trims.name: VX(O) 8S
trims.positioning: The sunroof and big screen with the eight-seat bench: the most car for the most people, literally.

trims.name: ZX
trims.positioning: The luxury Hycross: powered ottoman captain seats, quilted leather, 9-speaker JBL, dual-zone climate and a power back door. Seven seats only.

trims.name: ZX(O)
trims.positioning: The flagship adds what the ZX misses: adaptive cruise, lane tracing, blind spot monitor and the rest of Toyota Safety Sense. The only variant with ADAS.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: ADAS exists only on the top ZX(O), as Toyota Safety Sense with 6 functions. Every other variant, including the Rs 31.20 lakh ZX, goes without.

engines.name: 2.5L Dynamic Force Strong Hybrid
engines.torqueNote: 221 Nm is the engine's figure; the electric motor adds 208 Nm of its own
engines.character: Toyota's 5th generation hybrid with a lithium-ion battery: 230 PS when you push, near-silent electric crawling when you don't, and economy a small hatchback would envy

trims.name: Elegant
trims.positioning: The only trim, and it wants for nothing: 9 airbags, TSS 3.0, twin 12.3in screens, JBL, head-up display and a rear seat that reclines at the touch of its armrest.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: TSS 3.0 is standard but counts 5 functions here (adaptive cruise, lane tracing, lane departure, pre-collision, auto high beam); Toyota India's list does not include blind spot monitoring.

engines.name: 2.7L Petrol
engines.character: The quiet choice for short commutes and a dislike of diesel clatter: big, smooth and automatic only now, but the thirstiest way to run a Fortuner

engines.name: 2.8L Diesel
engines.torqueNote: 500 Nm with the 6AT; the 6MT runs a 420 Nm tune (official)
engines.character: The Fortuner most people buy: effortless torque for seven up and luggage, without paying for 4x4 hardware you may never use

engines.name: 2.8L Diesel 4x4
engines.torqueNote: 500 Nm with the 6AT; the 6MT runs a 420 Nm tune (official)
engines.character: The one for genuinely bad roads: proper low-range 4WD with a lockable diff, and the drivetrain the GR-S builds on

engines.name: 2.8L Diesel neoDrive 48V
engines.character: The same 2.8 diesel with a 48V helping hand: smoother starts, quieter idle stops and energy back under braking, though Toyota puts no number on the economy gain

trims.name: 4x2
trims.positioning: The full Fortuner from the first rupee: 7 airbags, ventilated leather seats, dual-zone climate and power front seats are all standard. You give up the 4x4 hardware and the JBL, not the luxury.

trims.name: 4x4
trims.positioning: The one built for the rough stuff: proper low range, a lockable rear diff, downhill assist, and the 11-speaker JBL Toyota saves for 4WD. Manual only unless you go Neo Drive.

trims.name: Legender
trims.positioning: The styled flagship line: split quad LED headlamps, sequential indicators, black roof, ambient lighting and a wireless charger. This 4x2 keeps 17in wheels and 6 speakers, so it is the look more than the kit.

trims.name: Neo Drive
trims.positioning: The 48V tech step on the 4x4 automatic: smoother starts, idle start-stop, Multi-Terrain Select and a wireless charger join the low-range hardware and JBL.

trims.name: Legender 4x4
trims.positioning: Legender style with the low-range hardware and JBL, sold with the manual gearbox. Worth knowing: the manual drops the wireless charger and the kick-sensor tailgate, and its diesel runs 420 Nm against the automatic's 500.

trims.name: Legender Neo Drive
trims.positioning: The complete Legender: 48V mild-hybrid diesel, Multi-Terrain Select, and the wireless charger and kick sensor back with the automatic. The flagship unless the GR badge calls you.

trims.name: GR-S
trims.positioning: The motorsport-flavoured flagship: GR grille, black alloys and a red-stitched black cabin on the plain diesel 4x4 automatic. You pay about Rs 2.17L over the Legender Neo Drive for the badge and the look, not for extra kit.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Fortuner on sale today offers ADAS at any price, Legender and GR-S included. Toyota Safety Sense arrives with the next generation, expected in India in 2027.

engines.name: 2.8L Diesel (4x2)
engines.character: The same 500 Nm workhorse driving the rear wheels only, for buyers who want the deck and the stance without the transfer case

engines.name: 2.8L Diesel (4x4)
engines.character: 204 PS, 500 Nm and a proper low-range transfer case: built to tow, wade and keep going long after soft-roaders turn back

trims.name: GX
trims.positioning: The honest workhorse: every airbag and the stability kit of the VX, an 8in screen, and nothing you would worry about scratching.

trims.name: VX
trims.positioning: The lifestyle Hilux: 12.3in screen, 360 camera, drive and terrain modes, cruise and connected tech. The AC is still manual, oddly.

engines.name: 2.5L Strong Hybrid e-CVT
engines.torqueNote: 240 Nm is the petrol engine's figure; Toyota publishes no separate motor torque for India
engines.character: Toyota's self-charging 2.5 hybrid moves this five-metre lounge in near silence and never needs a plug

trims.name: Hi
trims.positioning: Nobody's base car: massage captain seats with ottomans, 15 JBL speakers and the full safety suite. You give up the sunroof and rear screen.

trims.name: VIP Executive Lounge
trims.positioning: The chairman's spec: dual sunroof, head-up display, a 14in rear screen and the Executive Lounge chairs, for about Rs 10L more.

engines.name: 3.3L V6 Turbo Diesel
engines.character: 700 Nm of V6 diesel through a 10-speed auto: effortless in town, tireless across a desert, and famously hard to kill

trims.name: ZX
trims.positioning: The luxury reading: 20in alloys, chrome brightwork, illuminated side steps and a rear limited-slip differential. Every gadget is already here.

trims.name: GR-S
trims.positioning: The expedition reading: front and rear diff locks, a 31 degree approach angle on taller 18in rubber, GR-tuned suspension. Worth Rs 7.2L over the ZX only if you will actually leave the road.

models.name: Sonet
models.rearSuspension: Coupled torsion beam axle with coil spring

engines.name: 1.2L Smartstream Petrol
engines.character: Modest and easygoing around town; happiest below the top of the ladder, and it works hard when full

engines.name: 1.0L Smartstream T-GDi Turbo Petrol
engines.character: The keen one: strong mid-range punch, a proper clutchless iMT for three pedals' feel minus the legwork, or the quick 7DCT

engines.name: 1.5L CRDi VGT Diesel
engines.character: The distance runner: 250 Nm, the segment's only diesel torque-converter automatic, and easily the thriftiest Sonet

trims.name: HTE
trims.positioning: Honest base: the full 15-feature safety pack, 6 airbags and TPMS, but no audio system at all.

trims.name: HTE (O)
trims.positioning: The surprise rung: an electric sunroof this early, LED DRLs, and the cheapest way into the diesel.

trims.name: HTK (O)
trims.positioning: The volume step: 8in touchscreen with wireless CarPlay, rear camera, auto AC and the turbo's entry point.

trims.name: HTK+
trims.positioning: The plush step: crystal-cut alloys, wireless charger, smart key and the 60:40 split rear seat.

trims.name: HTK+ (O)
trims.positioning: Crown Jewel LED headlamps, leatherette seats and a factory-fit dual dashcam.

trims.name: HTX
trims.positioning: The gadget step: cruise, all-disc brakes, the air purifier, and ventilated seats on the automatics.

trims.name: GTX+
trims.positioning: The tech flagship: twin 10.25in screens, Bose audio, 360 camera and Level 1 ADAS.

trims.name: X-Line
trims.positioning: The GTX+ kit in Xclusive matte graphite with a sage green cabin: style, not extra features.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: The Sonet tops out at Level 1 ADAS, and only on the GTX+ and X-Line automatics; no Level 2 tier exists.

engines.name: 1.0L Smartstream G1.0 T-GDi Petrol
engines.character: Punchy little turbo triple: strong from low revs and relaxed on the highway, though it likes a careful right foot to hit its economy figure

engines.name: 1.5L D1.5 CRDi VGT Diesel
engines.character: The long-distance pick: effortless mid-range shove and the range's best economy with the manual, though the automatic drinks noticeably more

trims.name: HTE
trims.positioning: Safety-complete base: 6 airbags, ESC, TPMS and a 10.25in screen, but steel wheels and no camera.

trims.name: HTE (O)
trims.positioning: The cheapest sunroof in the range, plus 16-inch alloys and a height-adjust driver seat.

trims.name: HTK (EX)
trims.positioning: LED headlamps, the rear camera and roof rails arrive; the sensible floor for most buyers.

trims.name: HTK+
trims.positioning: The dual-pane panoramic sunroof, cruise control and a sliding, reclining rear bench.

trims.name: HTK+ (O)
trims.positioning: Leatherette seats and the rear wiper; the last trim you can have with a manual gearbox.

trims.name: HTX
trims.positioning: Automatic only: 17-inch alloys, the 12.3in screen, Harman Kardon, ventilated seats and a wireless charger.

trims.name: HTX (O)
trims.positioning: The flagship: Trinity display panel, Kia Connect 2.0, auto AC and rear ventilated seats.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: The 2026 Syros dropped ADAS entirely; no variant offers it, where the 2025 car's top trim had a Level 2 suite.

engines.name: Syros EV 42 kWh
engines.character: The sensible pack: 135 PS and a claimed 443 km, with the same 100 kW fast charging as the big battery

engines.name: Syros EV 51.4 kWh Extended Range
engines.character: The Extended Range pack: 171 PS, a claimed 526 km, and Kia's lifetime battery warranty for first owners

trims.name: HTK
trims.positioning: A generous base: twin 12.3in screens, auto AC, LED lamps and all-disc brakes, but no rear camera.

trims.name: HTK+
trims.positioning: The rear camera and cruise control arrive; the only mid trim you can pair with either battery.

trims.name: HTX
trims.positioning: The dual-pane panoramic sunroof and a sliding, reclining rear bench; the value sweet spot.

trims.name: HTX+
trims.positioning: Big battery only: leatherette, Harman Kardon, ventilated seats front and rear, wireless charger.

trims.name: X-Line
trims.positioning: The flagship, and the only trim with ADAS: Level 2 suite, 360 camera, V2L and ambient lighting.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: The Level 2 ADAS suite comes only on the top X-Line ER; every other Syros EV has none.

engines.name: Smartstream G1.5 Petrol
engines.character: Smooth and easygoing in town; pick it for ease and running costs rather than pace, with the IVT the relaxed choice

engines.name: Smartstream G1.5 T-GDi Turbo Petrol
engines.character: The quick one: 160 PS with a fast 7-speed DCT or a clutchless iMT, and the only engine on the top GTX(O) and X-Line(O) trims

engines.name: 1.5L CRDi VGT Diesel
engines.character: The long-distance pick: relaxed cruising torque and the lowest running costs, with a proper torque-converter automatic on offer

trims.name: HTE
trims.positioning: A base trim that keeps the good stuff: 6 airbags, 10.25in screen with wireless CarPlay, rear camera and cruise are all standard. You give up the split rear seat and the alloys, not the car.

trims.name: HTE(O)
trims.positioning: The livability step: semi-leatherette, 60:40 split rear seat with armrest, roof rails. Its automatics add drive and traction modes with an electronic parking brake.

trims.name: HTK
trims.positioning: Alloys and the daily conveniences: 17in wheels, auto-folding mirrors, rear wiper and defogger, rear sunshades, push-button start.

trims.name: HTK(O)
trims.positioning: The cheapest dual-pane panoramic sunroof in the range, with full leatherette, wireless charger, auto climate and front parking sensors.

trims.name: HTX
trims.positioning: Where the Seltos turns premium: 12.3in screen, Bose audio, dual-zone climate, ventilated seats, powered driver seat and 64-colour ambient lighting on every gearbox.

trims.name: HTX(A)
trims.positioning: The safety trim: Level 2 ADAS with 21 functions, 360 camera and the full Trinity display with a 12.3in digital cluster.

trims.name: GTX
trims.positioning: The GT-Line style trim: Ice Cube LED projectors, 18in alloys, 10-way memory driver seat. Note it skips the ADAS and 360 camera of the cheaper HTX(A).

trims.name: X-Line
trims.positioning: The GTX in its darkest suit: black alloys, gunmetal accents and exclusive matte paint. Style only, no new kit.

trims.name: GTX(A)
trims.positioning: The GT-Line look with the full safety stack: Level 2 ADAS, 360 camera and the 12.3in digital cluster join the 18in alloys and memory seat.

trims.name: X-Line(A)
trims.positioning: The GTX(A)'s kit in the darker X-Line styling: ADAS, 360 camera and digital cluster with black alloys and matte paint.

trims.name: GTX(O)
trims.positioning: The everything trim: ADAS grows to 28 functions with highway assist, plus head-up display, air purifier, dashcam, digital key and built-in navigation.

trims.name: X-Line(O)
trims.positioning: The flagship in the darkest trim: everything the GTX(O) carries, wrapped in black alloys and matte paint.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: ADAS starts at HTX(A): the (A) trims carry Level 2 with 21 functions and the top (O) trims 28. The style-led GTX and X-Line sit above HTX(A) on price but skip ADAS entirely.

engines.name: 1.5L Smartstream Petrol
engines.character: Does the job without drama and keeps the price honest, though seven aboard will have it working hard

engines.name: 1.5L CRDi VGT Diesel
engines.character: The one to pick for long miles: easy low-rev torque and cheaper running, for Rs 1.86 lakh more up front

engines.name: 1.5L Smartstream CNG
engines.character: The one to run on CNG money: keeps fuel bills down day to day, at the cost of a much smaller boot

trims.name: Premium (O)
trims.positioning: The one trim left: 6 airbags, an 8-inch screen with wireless CarPlay and roof vents for all three rows, at money the Clavis cannot match.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Carens has ADAS of any level. For that Kia points you at the Carens Clavis.
priorityNotes.panoramic-sunroof: No sunroof on the Carens at all; the skylight and panoramic roofs live in the Clavis range.

engines.name: 1.5L Smartstream Petrol
engines.character: Unhurried but honest: the budget way into the Clavis, happiest in town and never sold above the sunroof trims

engines.name: 1.5L T-GDi Turbo Petrol
engines.character: The keen one: 160 PS moves seven people without strain, and it is the only route to the DCT, the ADAS and the panoramic roof

engines.name: 1.5L CRDi VGT Diesel
engines.character: The distance runner: easy torque, the best economy in the range, and the only engine with the torque-converter automatic

engines.name: 1.5L Smartstream CNG
engines.character: The one to run on CNG money: keeps fuel bills down day to day, at the cost of a much smaller boot

trims.name: HTE
trims.positioning: The floor of the Clavis: 6 airbags, all-disc brakes and roof vents for both back rows, on steel wheels.

trims.name: HTE (O)
trims.positioning: Wireless CarPlay, a rear camera and auto headlamps: the sensible minimum for most families.

trims.name: HTE (EX)
trims.positioning: The cheapest sunroof in the range plus proper auto AC, and the only way to both on the 1.5 petrol.

trims.name: HTK+
trims.positioning: Alloys, roof rails, cruise and the smart key: where the Clavis starts feeling like the premium MPV Kia says it is.

trims.name: HTK+ (O)
trims.positioning: 17-inch alloys and a wireless charger, plus a no-cost captain-seat option on the automatics.

trims.name: HTX (Diesel)
trims.positioning: The diesel flagship: dual 12.25-inch screens, 360 camera and ambient lighting, though the panoramic roof stays petrol-only and you keep the single-pane sunroof.

trims.name: HTX
trims.positioning: The big tech jump: dual 12.25-inch screens, 360 camera, 64-colour ambient light and the dual-pane panoramic roof.

trims.name: HTX+
trims.positioning: Ventilated powered front seats, Bose sound and the air purifier: as plush as a manual Clavis gets.

trims.name: HTX (O)
trims.positioning: The cheaper route to the DCT: Bose, drive modes and the parking brake by wire, without HTX+ money.

trims.name: GTX
trims.positioning: The GT-Line: HTX (O) kit in the sportier body kit with LED fog lamps and lime calipers, though the Bose system is not part of the deal.

trims.name: HTX (O) A
trims.positioning: HTX (O) plus the full Level 2 ADAS suite: the cheapest driver assistance in a Clavis.

trims.name: HTX+ DCT
trims.positioning: The full HTX+ kit with the automatic, which is also what unlocks Level 2 ADAS and drive modes.

trims.name: GTX+
trims.positioning: The 6-seat captain-chair flagship in GT-Line dress: everything the Clavis offers, sportier trimmings on top.

trims.name: X-Line
trims.positioning: The same flagship kit in X-Line black, with the exclusive Dark Gun Metal paint and a 7-seat bench.

priorityNotes.panoramic-sunroof: The dual-pane panoramic roof is turbo-petrol only. Diesel buyers top out at the single-pane sunroof, and the 1.5 petrol stops at the HTE (EX) skylight.
priorityNotes.safety-adas: Level 2 ADAS comes only with the DCT automatic, on HTX (O) A, HTX+ DCT, GTX+ and X-Line. No manual Clavis has it.

engines.name: 42 kWh Electric
engines.character: The value pack: 135 PS and a claimed 404 km, the cheapest way into an electric three-row family car

engines.name: 51.4 kWh Electric (Extended Range)
engines.character: The extended range pack: 171 PS and a claimed 490 km, the one that makes school runs all week and a highway weekend a no-charge affair

trims.name: HTK+
trims.positioning: Honest base: 6 airbags, both 12.25in screens, full LED lamps and i-Pedal regen on 16in alloys.

trims.name: HTX E
trims.positioning: The comfort step: panoramic sunroof, leatherette, wireless charger, air purifier and the no-cost captain-seat option.

trims.name: HTX
trims.positioning: The safety step: the roughly 20-function Level 2 ADAS suite, 360 camera and blind view monitor.

trims.name: GTX
trims.positioning: GT Line styling on HTX kit: black high-gloss trim, lime calipers and metal pedals, nothing extra on the spec sheet.

trims.name: HTX+
trims.positioning: The luxury step: ventilated front seats, Bose audio, rain-sensing wipers and V2L to power your gear.

trims.name: GTX+
trims.positioning: GT Line flagship: everything on HTX+ plus Digital Key, a battery heater and the sporty look.

trims.name: X-Line
trims.positioning: The rugged flagship: GTX+ kit under matte Dark Gun Metal styling you cannot have on any other trim.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: Level 2 ADAS starts at HTX. HTK+ and HTX E go without it, whichever battery you pick.
priorityNotes.captain-seats: From HTX E up, the 6-seat captain layout costs the same as the 7-seat bench; you choose at booking. HTK+ is 7-seat only.

engines.name: 2.2L Smartstream CRDi Diesel
engines.character: Effortless rather than exciting: 441 Nm and a smooth 8-speed auto built to waft seven people and their luggage across states

trims.name: Limousine Plus
trims.positioning: The only trim, and it holds nothing back: 8 airbags, Level 2 ADAS, powered VIP recliners, Bose and both 12.3in screens.

engines.name: 84 kWh Dual Motor AWD Electric
engines.character: An 800V dual-motor flagship: 325 PS, a claimed 663 km, 10 to 80 percent in 18 minutes on the right charger, and V2L to run your appliances

trims.name: GT-Line AWD
trims.positioning: The only trim sold here, and it is the full kit: 27-function ADAS 2.0, Meridian audio, AR head-up display, V2L and relaxation seats.

engines.name: 99.8 kWh Dual Motor AWD Electric
engines.character: A 384 PS three-row flagship: a claimed 561 km, 10 to 80 percent in 24 minutes on the right charger, and it moves six people in massage seats

trims.name: GT-Line AWD
trims.positioning: The only trim sold here, and it is the full kit: 10 airbags, 27-function Level 2 ADAS, massage captain seats, Meridian audio and V2L.

engines.name: 2.2L Smartstream CRDi Diesel
engines.character: The familiar choice: 442 Nm from Kia's well-proven diesel, built for the miles a three-row SUV is actually bought to cover

engines.name: 2.2L Smartstream CRDi Diesel AWD
engines.character: The same diesel with all-wheel drive and terrain modes added, for the HTX buyer who wants the badge's ability to match its size

engines.name: 1.6L Smartstream Turbo GDI Hybrid
engines.character: The efficiency pick: a turbo-petrol engine and an electric motor sharing the work, without ever needing a plug

engines.name: 1.6L Smartstream Turbo GDI Hybrid AWD
engines.character: The hybrid with AWD and terrain modes for the HTX tier, pairing the efficiency case with all-wheel security

trims.name: HTE
trims.positioning: The entry point into Kia's first three-row SUV in India: 7 airbags, a 12.3in touchscreen, wireless charging and dual-zone climate as standard, seven seats only.

trims.name: HTK
trims.positioning: The value pick of the ladder: twin 12.3in displays, a 12-speaker Bose system, a panoramic sunroof, front ventilated seats and the 360 camera, still on front-wheel drive.

trims.name: HTK 6-seat
trims.positioning: HTK's kit in a 6-seat, second-row captain-chair layout instead of the 7-seat bench.

trims.name: HTK(A)
trims.positioning: HTK's kit plus a smaller Level 2 ADAS package, still on front-wheel drive. Diesel only; added 2026-09-14.

trims.name: HTK(A) 6-seat
trims.positioning: HTK(A)'s kit in a 6-seat, second-row captain-chair layout instead of the 7-seat bench.

trims.name: HTX
trims.positioning: AWD standard with Snow/Sand/Mud terrain modes, 10 airbags, front and rear ventilated seats and a head-up display, one step below the ADAS package.

trims.name: HTX(A)
trims.positioning: The top of the ladder this file models: everything HTX has, plus Kia's largest ADAS package on this car. Diesel AWD 7-seat only, added 2026-09-13; see header for the other HTX(A) configurations still not confirmed.

engines.name: 1.5L D117 CRDe Diesel
engines.character: The affordable way into a Thar: enough torque for the look and the lifestyle, without the 4WD hardware or its running costs

engines.name: 2.2L D22 mHawk Diesel (RWD)
engines.character: The new one: mHawk torque and an automatic, without the low-range hardware or its weight and thirst

engines.name: 2.2L D22 mHawk Diesel (4WD)
engines.character: The classic Thar combination: unstressed diesel torque, low-range 4WD, and the best long-trip economy of the range

engines.name: 2.0L G20 TGDi mStallion Petrol (RWD)
engines.character: The easy-driving Thar: quick, refined and automatic only, for buyers who want the shape more than the mud

engines.name: 2.0L G20 TGDi mStallion Petrol (4WD)
engines.character: The quickest Thar, with proper low-range 4WD: revvy on the road, thirsty when you use it

trims.name: AXT
trims.positioning: The bare-bones Thar: dual airbags, ESC and hill descent, but no screen and no speakers. Hard top only, RWD diesel only.

trims.name: LXT
trims.positioning: The Thar most people mean: 10.25in touchscreen, reverse camera, cruise and 18in alloys, with every engine and the 4WD hardware on offer. Hard top only since the convertible was dropped in April 2025.

trims.name: ZXT
trims.positioning: The one to have if you want the safety kit: six airbags and disc brakes on all four wheels, plus 19in alloys, LED headlamps and the softer-riding dampers. The step up from the same LXT runs from about Rs 50,000 to about Rs 1.3 lakh depending on which engine and gearbox you pick, so it is worth checking your own combination rather than assuming.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No Thar 3-door variant offers ADAS at any price.

engines.name: 2.0L mStallion Turbo Petrol (RWD)
engines.torqueNote: Automatic cars run a stronger 177 PS / 380 Nm tune
engines.character: Quick and refined for the road-going Roxx; the automatic's stronger tune makes it the enthusiast pick, at a fuel cost

engines.name: 2.2L mHawk Diesel (RWD)
engines.torqueNote: Automatic cars run a stronger 175 PS / 370 Nm tune
engines.character: The everyday Roxx: big easy torque, the range's best economy, and no 4WD hardware to pay for or carry around

engines.name: 2.2L mHawk Diesel (4WD)
engines.torqueNote: Automatic cars run a stronger 175 PS / 370 Nm tune (official: 128.6 kW / 370 Nm)
engines.character: The full-fat Roxx: proper low-range 4WD with a locking rear diff and 650 mm wading, for buyers who will actually leave the tarmac

trims.name: MX1
trims.positioning: Honest base: 6 airbags, ESC, LED projectors and the 10.25in screen, though the screen mirrors no phone here.

trims.name: MX3
trims.positioning: The sensible step: rear camera, cruise, wireless charger, wireless Android Auto and the drive and terrain modes.

trims.name: AX3L
trims.positioning: The tech track: Level 2 ADAS, digital cluster and connected car tech on the diesel manual, but none of MX5's comfort kit.

trims.name: MX5
trims.positioning: The comfort track: sunroof, leatherette, alloys and TPMS, and the cheapest way into the 4WD hardware. No ADAS here.

trims.name: AX5L
trims.positioning: The first trim with both tracks: MX5's comfort plus Level 2 ADAS and connected tech. Diesel automatic only.

trims.name: AX7L
trims.positioning: Fully loaded: panoramic roof, 360 camera, ventilated seats, powered driver seat and the Harman Kardon system.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: Level 2 ADAS is exclusive to the diesel-only AX L trims (AX3L, AX5L, AX7L); no petrol Roxx offers it.

engines.name: 2.0L mStallion Turbo Petrol
engines.torqueNote: 370 Nm with the manual, 380 Nm with the automatic
engines.character: Strong and quick for something this size, and the cheapest way in, but it drinks: the diesel is the one most buyers should shortlist

engines.name: 2.2L mHawk Diesel (132 PS)
engines.character: The workhorse tune on the Z2 and Z4 manuals, and nothing else: unhurried but easy torque, built for a full cabin rather than a fast overtake

engines.name: 2.2L mHawk Diesel (175 PS)
engines.torqueNote: 370 Nm with the manual, 400 Nm with the automatic
engines.character: The default Scorpio-N engine from Z6 up: big easy torque, relaxed cruising and the best economy in the range

engines.name: 2.2L mHawk Diesel (175 PS) 4XPLOR 4WD
engines.torqueNote: 370 Nm with the manual, 400 Nm with the automatic
engines.character: The same 175 PS diesel with shift-on-fly 4XPLOR four-wheel drive, terrain modes and a mechanical locking rear differential: pick it for genuinely bad roads, not for the badge

trims.name: Z2
trims.positioning: The honest base: the full 5-star body, dual airbags, four speakers and steel wheels. Halogen lamps and manual AC tell you where the money went, and there is no phone mirroring at all.

trims.name: Z4
trims.positioning: The everyday kit step, and the first one you can plug a phone into: the 8in screen gains wired Android Auto and CarPlay, plus cruise control, a height-adjust seat with lumbar, a rear wiper and roof rails.

trims.name: Z6
trims.positioning: Diesel-only middle child: a sunroof, a reversing camera, six speakers, drive modes and the 175 PS engine arrive here. Still on steel wheels, though.

trims.name: Z8S
trims.positioning: Where the cabin changes character: a 12.3in screen and a full digital cluster, six airbags, LED projectors, connected tech with Alexa, an emergency call button and the first alloy wheels.

trims.name: Z8
trims.positioning: The comfort pass: dual-zone climate, keyless entry with push-button start, auto headlamps and wipers, tyre pressure monitoring and a cooled wireless charger.

trims.name: Z8T
trims.positioning: Nearly everything the flagship has except the driver aids: the 12-speaker Sony system, R18 alloys, ventilated seats, a powered driver seat and an electronic parking brake. It is also the first rung you can have with 4WD.

trims.name: Z8L
trims.positioning: The flagship, and the only Scorpio-N with the panoramic skyroof, the 540 degree camera and Level 2 ADAS. Adaptive cruise and Smart Pilot Assist need the automatic.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: Level 2 ADAS exists only on the top Z8L, and its adaptive cruise and Smart Pilot Assist work only with the automatic. Every other trim has none, though the Z8S and up do give you six airbags and an emergency call button.
priorityNotes.panoramic-sunroof: The panoramic skyroof arrived with Mahindra's August 2026 update and only the top Z8L has it. Z6 through Z8T carry a single-pane sunroof instead, and the Z2 and Z4 have none.

engines.name: 2.2L mHawk Diesel
engines.character: The one and only engine: an unstressed 2.2 diesel with a 6-speed manual, happier hauling a full bench than chasing a gap in traffic

trims.name: S
trims.positioning: The bare-bones workhorse: vinyl seats, halogen lamps, steel wheels and no touchscreen. Also the only way to the 9-seat layout.

trims.name: S11
trims.positioning: The only other rung, and a big step: 9in touchscreen, climate control, LED lamps, alloys and roof rails. Still no automatic, camera or sunroof at any price.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: The Scorpio Classic has no ADAS, no ESC claim and no automatic option at any price. If driver aids matter to you, look at the Scorpio-N instead.
priorityNotes.panoramic-sunroof: No Scorpio Classic has a sunroof of any kind.

engines.name: 1.5L mHawk75 Diesel
engines.character: Slow by modern standards but built to lug: the torque arrives low and it shrugs off bad roads and full benches

trims.name: B4
trims.positioning: The working base: vinyl seats, no touchscreen, no power windows, but the same frame and engine as the rest.

trims.name: B6
trims.positioning: Where most buyers should start: power windows, central locking, remote key and the 7-inch screen arrive here.

trims.name: B6 Opt
trims.positioning: Adds fog lamps, a rear wiper and washer, bending headlamps and trip info; the pick for daily highway miles.

trims.name: B8
trims.positioning: The new flagship: diamond-cut alloys and leatherette, the dressiest a Bolero has ever been.

engines.name: 1.5L mHawk100 Diesel
engines.character: Usefully stronger than the classic Bolero's engine: relaxed at highway speeds and happy with seven aboard

trims.name: N4
trims.positioning: Vinyl seats and no music system, but power windows all round and the full 100 PS engine from the start.

trims.name: N8
trims.positioning: Fabric seats, a basic music player, remote key and a rear wiper; the honest middle of the range.

trims.name: N10 (R)
trims.positioning: The sweet spot: 9-inch screen with rear camera, cruise, ISOFIX, alloys and a height-adjustable seat.

trims.name: N11
trims.positioning: The dressy one: leatherette, 16-inch alloys and dual-tone paint over N10 (R), with no extra hardware.

trims.name: N10 Opt
trims.positioning: The capable one: N10 (R) plus a locking rear differential for genuinely bad roads; fabric seats stay.

engines.name: 2.2L mHawk Diesel
engines.character: The big 2.2 from the Scorpio family: effortless with all nine seats filled, and never working hard on the highway

trims.name: P4
trims.positioning: The people-mover base: all nine seats, power windows and ISOFIX, but no touchscreen and steel wheels.

trims.name: P10
trims.positioning: The 9-inch screen, speakers worth having and alloys for Rs 1.10L more; the one private buyers pick.

engines.name: 1.2L mStallion TCMPFi Turbo Petrol
engines.character: The everyday turbo petrol: smooth, adequate and the cheapest way in; the lower trims are all built around it.

engines.name: 1.2L mStallion TGDi Turbo Petrol
engines.character: The quick one, reserved for the upper trims: 131 PS of segment-topping punch that suits the 6-speed automatic best.

engines.name: 1.5L CRDe Turbo Diesel
engines.character: The distance runner: 300 Nm and the best certified economy in the range, for buyers who count kilometres.

trims.name: MX1
trims.positioning: The honest base: 6 airbags, ESC, all-disc brakes and projector lamps, but no touchscreen.

trims.name: MX2
trims.positioning: The screen step, sold as the cheapest diesel: 10.25in touchscreen and 4 speakers.

trims.name: MX2 Pro
trims.positioning: MX2 plus the single-pane sunroof: the cheapest way to open the roof.

trims.name: MX3
trims.positioning: The tech-per-rupee pick: Bi-LED projectors, wireless Android Auto, cruise control.

trims.name: REVX EDGE
trims.positioning: A value pick, not a strict step up from MX3: keeps MX3's bi-halogen headlamps rather than upgrading, but adds a rear camera, a height-adjustable driver's seat, a rear armrest and leatherette seats MX3 does not have at any price.

trims.name: MX3 Pro
trims.positioning: MX3 with the sunroof: the last stop before the big AX5 jump.

trims.name: REVX EDGE (O)
trims.positioning: REVX EDGE plus a panoramic sunroof, roof rails, auto-folding ORVMs, auto headlamps and rain-sensing wipers, for well under what AX5 asks for the same roof and lamps.

trims.name: AX5
trims.positioning: The volume trim: twin 10.25in screens, dual-zone climate, alloys, connected tech, rear camera.

trims.name: AX5 L
trims.positioning: The safety branch: Level 2 ADAS, 360 camera and wireless charging without the AX7's plusher kit.

trims.name: AX7

trims.positioning: ZXi with one addition, the panoramic sunroof; pay for it only if you want it.

trims.name: ZXi+
trims.positioning: The tech flagship: Level 2 ADAS, 360 camera, ventilated seats, Dolby Atmos.

trims.name: ZXi+ (O)
trims.positioning: Everything the Victoris offers, panoramic sunroof included.

trims.name: VXi (Strong Hybrid)
trims.positioning: The affordable door into the 28.65 km/l strong hybrid, with VXi kit.

trims.name: ZXi (Strong Hybrid)
trims.positioning: ZXi comfort with the self-charging drivetrain; the value hybrid pick.

trims.name: ZXi (O) (Strong Hybrid)
trims.positioning: The hybrid ZXi plus the panoramic sunroof.

trims.name: ZXi+ (Strong Hybrid)
trims.positioning: Full ADAS-and-Atmos kit married to the economy-champion drivetrain.

trims.name: ZXi+ (O) (Strong Hybrid)
trims.positioning: The complete Victoris: strong hybrid, ADAS, Atmos and the big sunroof.

engines.name: 1.0 K10C Petrol
engines.character: Easygoing 3-cylinder that suits city errands; happiest below highway overtaking speeds.

engines.name: 1.2 K-Series DualJet Petrol
engines.character: The engine to have if you tour: usefully stronger than the 1.0 for a small price step.

engines.name: 1.0 K10C S-CNG
engines.character: Rock-bottom running costs for high-mileage city use; noticeably down on power on gas.

trims.name: LXi
trims.positioning: The price leader: all six airbags and ESP, but bare enough that most buyers step up.

trims.name: VXi
trims.positioning: The sensible floor: power windows, keyless entry and basic audio; the trim most CNG buyers pick.

trims.name: ZXi
trims.positioning: Where the 1.2 engine and the touchscreen arrive together; the pick if you carry the family often.

trims.name: ZXi+
trims.positioning: The loaded one: folding mirrors, rear wiper, split rear seat, plus the dual-tone look on options.

engines.name: 1.5L K15C Smart Hybrid Petrol
engines.character: Relaxed six-seater cruiser; adequate rather than quick, with mild-hybrid assist helping in traffic

engines.name: 1.5L K15C S-CNG
engines.character: The high-mileage school-run special; noticeably down on power with all six seats filled

trims.name: Zeta
trims.positioning: Already generous for a base: captain seats, LED lamps, cruise and auto AC.

trims.name: Alpha
trims.positioning: The sweet spot: wireless CarPlay, 360 camera, Arkamys sound and leatherette.

trims.name: Alpha+
trims.positioning: Tops out with ventilated front seats, head-up display and TPMS.

engines.name: 59.6 kWh Electric (130 kW)
engines.character: The Earth's motor: down 20 kW on the Wind but with 5 km more certified range, and the calmer pick for city work

engines.name: 59.6 kWh Electric (150 kW)
engines.character: The stronger tune on the same 59.6 kWh pack: 310 Nm makes it the quicker car, for 5 km of certified range

trims.name: Earth
trims.positioning: Base trim with the range advantage: 360 camera, 7 airbags and the full 12.9 inch screen, on the thriftier 130 kW motor.

trims.name: Wind
trims.positioning: The tech step: Level 2 ADAS with rear AEB, HUD, ventilated seats and the 150 kW motor arrive together.

trims.name: Wind Infinity
trims.positioning: Wind plus a fixed edge-to-edge panoramic glass roof; the equipment is otherwise identical.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: Level 2 ADAS with front and rear AEB starts at Wind; the Earth trim has none. All trims carry 7 airbags and a 360 camera.

engines.name: 59.6 kWh Electric (130 kW)
engines.character: The entry pack: the same motor as the smaller VF 6 hauling a bigger car, so it is the calm, price-led choice

engines.name: 70 kWh Electric (150 kW)
engines.character: The long-legged pack: 532 km certified is the headline of the range, and the one for intercity work

engines.name: 70 kWh Dual Motor AWD
engines.character: The performance pick: twin motors, all-wheel drive and 0-100 in 5.8 seconds, trading 22 km of certified range for it

trims.name: Earth
trims.positioning: Base trim that skimps on little: HUD, dual-zone AC, 360 camera and 19 inch alloys are all standard, on the 59.6 kWh pack.

trims.name: Wind
trims.positioning: The long-range tech step: the 70 kWh pack, Level 2 ADAS with driver monitoring, ventilated seats and a powered tailgate.

trims.name: Wind Infinity
trims.positioning: Wind plus a fixed edge-to-edge panoramic glass roof; the equipment is otherwise identical.

trims.name: Sky
trims.positioning: Wind's kit with the dual-motor AWD drivetrain: 260 kW, 500 Nm and 0-100 in 5.8 seconds.

trims.name: Sky Infinity
trims.positioning: The full car: Sky's AWD drivetrain under the fixed panoramic glass roof.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: Level 2 ADAS with driver monitoring starts at Wind; the Earth trim has none. All trims carry 7 airbags and a 360 camera.

engines.name: 60.13 kWh Electric
engines.character: One tune for one job: 517 km certified from a mid-size pack, because an MPV is bought for distance per rupee, not pace

trims.name: VF MPV 7
trims.positioning: One fully-loaded spec: seven real seats, third-row AC with its own controls, and 1,240 litres with the rows folded.

priorityNotes.safety-adas: No ADAS on this car, and 4 airbags against the 7 of its VinFast SUV stablemates. Rear camera and full stability suite are standard.

engines.name: 49.92 kWh Blade Battery Electric
engines.character: The smaller Blade pack: 468 km claimed and 0 to 100 in 7.9 seconds, which is plenty unless you regularly run long

engines.name: 60.48 kWh Blade Battery Electric
engines.character: The long-range Blade pack: 521 km claimed, 0 to 100 in 7.3 seconds and quicker DC charging

trims.name: Dynamic
trims.positioning: The way in, and it is far from stripped: panoramic sunroof, 360 camera, powered driver's seat and the 12.8-inch rotating screen are all here. What you give up is range and the driver aids.

trims.name: Premium
trims.positioning: Buys the bigger battery, which is the point: 521 km claimed instead of 468, faster DC charging, 18-inch wheels and a powered tailgate.

trims.name: Superior
trims.positioning: The only ATTO 3 with driver aids. Adaptive cruise, autonomous braking and blind-spot warning arrive together, along with ventilated front seats, eight speakers and a seventh airbag.

engines.name: 71.8 kWh Blade Battery Electric (120 kW)
engines.character: The softer of the two: 485 km claimed on the Indian cycle, and 0 to 100 in 10.1 seconds with seven people aboard the same 71.8 kWh pack

engines.name: 71.8 kWh Blade Battery Electric (150 kW)
engines.character: Same battery, more motor: 0 to 100 in 8.6 seconds, and a 530 km claim measured on the gentler NEDC cycle

trims.name: Comfort
trims.positioning: The sensible one: six airbags, 360 camera, captain chairs and the 12.8-inch rotating screen for the least money. You adjust the seats by hand and there is no glass roof.

trims.name: Superior
trims.positioning: Rs 1.40 lakh more brings the driver aids, the panoramic glass roof, ventilated and powered front seats, wireless charging and the stronger 150 kW motor.

engines.name: 61.44 kWh Blade Battery Electric
engines.character: The smaller Blade pack, still rear-driven and still good for 0 to 100 in 7.5 seconds. A claimed 510 km on the optimistic NEDC cycle, so plan on rather less

engines.name: 82.56 kWh Blade Battery Electric
engines.character: The long-range pack and a stronger rear motor: 0 to 100 in 5.9 seconds and the longest claimed range in the range, though on the optimistic NEDC cycle

engines.name: 82.56 kWh Blade Battery Electric AWD
engines.character: Two motors and 0 to 100 in 3.8 seconds, which is supercar territory for the money. The extra motor costs about 70 km of claimed range against the rear-drive car

trims.name: Dynamic
trims.positioning: The entry car, and it is not stripped out: you already get every driver aid BYD fits, the rotating 15.6 inch screen, 12 Dynaudio speakers and ventilated front seats. What you give up is range.

trims.name: Premium
trims.positioning: Rs 4.70 lakh buys the big battery and 140 km more claimed range, plus a head-up display, seat memory, adaptive damping, real leather and 19 inch wheels. The sensible pick if you drive far.

trims.name: Performance
trims.positioning: A second motor on the front axle takes it to 0 to 100 in 3.8 seconds, with DiSus-C damping and torque vectoring to match. You pay Rs 7.45 lakh over Premium and lose 70 km of claimed range for it.

engines.name: 71.8 kWh Blade Battery Electric
engines.character: The smaller Blade pack, and still 0 to 100 in 7.3 seconds. A claimed 520 km on the optimistic NEDC cycle, so plan on rather less

engines.name: 82.56 kWh Blade Battery Electric
engines.character: The long-range pack with a stronger rear motor: 0 to 100 in 6.7 seconds, the furthest this car claims to go, and 11 kW home charging to refill it overnight

engines.name: 82.56 kWh Blade Battery Electric AWD
engines.character: Two motors, 690 Nm and 0 to 100 in 4.5 seconds from a two-and-a-third tonne SUV. The front motor costs about 25 km of claimed range

trims.name: Dynamic
trims.positioning: The entry car, and the only one on the smaller battery. You still get 11 airbags, the full driver-aid suite, the rotating 15.6 inch screen and a Dynaudio system, but the cabin is the plainest of the three.

trims.name: Premium
trims.positioning: Rs 8 lakh over the Dynamic buys the big battery, 47 km more claimed range, faster 11 kW home charging and the cabin most people picture: leather, seat memory, a head-up display and mood lighting.

trims.name: Performance
trims.positioning: A second motor takes it to 0 to 100 in 4.5 seconds on 20 inch wheels. Rs 6 lakh over Premium, and it costs you 25 km of claimed range for the privilege.

engines.name: Premium Rear-Wheel Drive
engines.character: One rear motor, 500 km on the WLTP cycle and 0 to 100 in 5.9 seconds, with 175 kW charging that adds about 238 km in a quarter of an hour

trims.name: Premium
trims.positioning: The only Model Y Tesla sells here, so there is no next trim to weigh up. Everything is in it: ventilated front seats, nine speakers, the HEPA filter and the full glass roof.

engines.name: Premium Dual Motor All-Wheel Drive
engines.character: Two motors and all-wheel drive: 681 km on the WLTP cycle, 0 to 100 in 5.0 seconds, and 250 kW charging that adds about 288 km in a quarter of an hour

trims.name: Premium
trims.positioning: The only Model Y L Tesla sells, and the reason to pick it over the five-seater is the third row: six seats, adaptive dampers, 18 speakers and 681 km of claimed range.
